dimension: INSTALL + INIT on a repo that already has a harness
summary: I copied the proyecto_ui replica to $SANDBOX/batten-testbed/run-init/proyecto_ui, exported BATTEN_DB to the sandbox, and ran `batten init --scan-json`, `batten init`, `batten init` twice, `batten init --from`, and `batten doctor`, plus controlled mutations of the generated spec to probe doctor. The scan is genuinely good at the structural part: it found all 4 domains and their AGENTS.md, put the whole harness (root AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md + 4 per-domain files) at the top of the generated file with the right framing ("the spec must agree with it, not replace it"), detected graphify and engram, refused to overwrite an existing batten.yaml, and emitted six honest notes[] about exactly what it could not derive. `doctor` is similarly honest: it flags the empty QA gate as verifying NOTHING, flags report mode, and catches a missing rules file, a nonexistent skill and a nonexistent agent. Nothing was written outside the sandbox (`git status --porcelain` in the repo shows only `?? batten.yaml`) and every batten invocation used the sandbox store (doctor printed `✓ store: .../run-init/state.db`). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the prebuilt binary is stale relative to the source repo. batten.exe was built 2026-07-27 23:52; internal/scan/scan.go was last written 2026-07-28 00:06, and commits 3122d29 ("init reads the backlog for the unit, not just branch names") and d99b6ef ("skill suggestions match a skill's name, never its prose") already fix findings 4 and 5 below. I reproduced both against the binary I was told to use, and I mark them as fixed-at-HEAD rather than pretending they are open. Findings 1,2,3,6,7,9,10 I verified are still present in the HEAD source. One thing I read in the new code but could NOT reproduce (binary is stale, I was told not to rebuild) and therefore do not list as a finding: the backlog also contains US-UX-01..US-UX-08 headings; pickUnit's regex `([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9})-(\d{1,6})` reads those as prefix "UX", so "US" wins on count and the emitted pattern would be `US-\d{3}`, which cannot match `US-UX-01` — 8 of the 44 backlog items would be invisible to batten. Worth a test at HEAD.
worked: All 4 domains detected with the right path and rules file. `batten init` printed `4 domain(s) detected` and the spec contains backend/, db/, frontend/, ml/ each with `rules: <dir>/AGENTS.md`. No false domains from docs/, data/ or context/.

The full pre-existing harness is surfaced, not ignored. batten.yaml opens with a 9-line comment block listing AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and all four per-domain AGENTS.md with the note 'This repo ALREADY has a process. The spec below should agree with it, not replace it'. scan.json's harness[] adds 'per-directory rules — this boundary is probably a fan-out axis, and these are its invariants'.

`batten init` refuses to overwrite. Second run: `batten: batten.yaml already exists — remove it or edit it by hand`, EXIT=1, and md5sum of batten.yaml was byte-identical before (db819a6568e6cc580d7699656496f570) and after.

The empty QA gate is warned about in three places. scan.json notes[]: 'NO check command was found — gates.qa.checks is empty, which means the gate currently verifies nothing. Fill it before flipping enforcement to enforce'; the same line is echoed as a comment at the bottom of batten.yaml; and `batten doctor` prints `⚠ gate "qa" declares no checks — it verifies NOTHING and approves on the agent's word.`

Every domain got `check: []   # TODO: no build/test command auto-detected` rather than a fabricated command. With no Makefile/pyproject/package.json in the replica, inventing `make test` would have been worse.

Capability detection is correct. `graphify found, engram found`; doctor prints `✓ graph: graphify (on PATH)` plus `⚠ no graphify-out/graph.json yet` and `· memory: engram (via MCP; batten does not store episodic memory)`.

doctor catches a renamed/missing skill exactly as batten.schema.json promises: after editing db's skills list I got `⚠ domains.db.skills references "this-skill-does-not-exist", which is not installed`.
doctor catches a missing agent: `⚠ domains.db.agent references "no-such-agent", which is not installed`, and a missing rules file: `⚠ domain "backend": rules file missing: nope/AGENTS.md`.

Unit inference does work when the signal it looks at is present. In a copy where I ran `git checkout -b feature/E2-US-015-auth-jwt`, `batten init` printed `unit="US"` and emitted `name: US` / `pattern: 'US-\d{3}'`. The TASK-N default is a sourcing gap, not a broken regex.

Isolation held. `git status --porcelain` in the sandbox repo shows only `?? batten.yaml`; state.db (118 KB) was created under run-init/ and doctor confirmed `✓ store: .../run-init/state.db`. I never referenced $HOME/Proyectos/MNA/proyecto_ui or the OneDrive vault, never ran git push, and the generated spec's capabilities.obsidian.vault is the empty string.

findings.title: `batten init --help` writes batten.yaml instead of printing help; every unknown flag is silently swallowed
findings.command: cd <sandbox>/run-init/proyecto_ui && export BATTEN_DB=<sandbox>/run-init/state.db && <testbed>/batten.exe init --help; echo "EXIT=$?"; ls batten.yaml
findings.observed:
wrote batten.yaml — a working draft in report mode (gates warn, don't block).
  project="proyecto_ui" unit="TASK", 4 domain(s) detected, graphify found, engram found
Next:
  1. fill the invariants (the TODOs) — the highest-value part of the file
  2. run: batten doctor
  3. flip enforcement: enforce when you trust the gates
For a richer draft (invariants mined from AGENTS.md, migration from a prose doc),
run /batten-init inside Claude Code instead — it uses `batten init --scan-json`.
EXIT=0
batten.yaml

Same for `init -h` and `init --bogus-flag`. This was literally my first batten command of the run: I asked for help and got a file in the repo.
findings.expected: `--help`/`-h` prints the init usage (the flags are `--scan-json` and `--from <doc>`) and exits 0 without writing anything. An unrecognised flag prints `unknown flag: --bogus-flag` and exits non-zero.
findings.why_it_matters: `--help` is the universally safe first probe of an unfamiliar CLI. Here it is a write. It cannot clobber an existing spec (the overwrite guard fires first), but on first contact with a repo it silently creates a tracked-file-to-be that the user did not ask for and may not notice — and it teaches the user that this binary ignores its own flags, which is exactly the wrong lesson right before they type `--from`.
findings.file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go (func cmdInit, lines ~1429-1440: the arg loop has only `case "--scan-json"` and `case "--from"`, no default)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `default:` arm returning `fmt.Errorf("unknown flag %q", args[i])`, and an explicit `case "--help", "-h":` that prints usage and returns nil. Same treatment for the other cmdX(os.Args[2:]) entry points.

findings.title: `batten init --from <doc>` never reads the doc — it only prints its own argument back
findings.command: cd <sandbox>/run-init/fromtest && git init -q . && <testbed>/batten.exe init --from context/planeacion_proyecto.md   # then: diff fromtest/batten.yaml flagtest/batten.yaml
findings.observed:
The generated batten.yaml is byte-identical to one produced by plain `batten init` in an empty dir — `diff` reports only `3c3 < project: fromtest --- > project: flagtest`. unit is still `name: TASK / pattern: 'TASK-\d+'`, there is no `unit.plan`, no `unit.locator`, no gates, no invariants. The only effect of --from is one extra stdout line: `  2. reconcile against your prose workflow: context/planeacion_proyecto.md`.

It also accepts a path that does not exist, with exit 0:
  $ batten.exe init --from does-not-exist.md
  ...
    2. reconcile against your prose workflow: does-not-exist.md
  EXIT=0
findings.expected: Either (a) --from actually mines the prose doc as DESIGN.md §'loom init — el arranque que hace que esto sea usable' promises ('`loom init --from docs/general/prompts_optimizers_v2.local.md` → **lee tu flujo en prosa y propone el `loom.yaml`**'), or at minimum (b) it records the path as `unit.plan:` in the spec — the key exists in batten.schema.json and README line 107 shows `plan: docs/backlog.md` — and (c) it errors out when the file does not exist.
findings.why_it_matters: `batten --help` advertises `batten init [--from <prose-doc>]` and DESIGN.md calls it the migration path, with the note that '`loom init` mediocre = producto muerto ... es la feature más importante'. A user pointing --from at their 1500-line planning doc gets a file that contains not one fact from it and no signal that nothing happened. Silently accepting a nonexistent path removes the last chance to notice.
findings.file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go (func cmdInit: `from` is captured at line ~1437 and used only at line ~1475 in a Printf)
findings.suggested_fix: Short term: os.Stat the path and fail loudly if missing; set facts.UnitPlan = from so the spec at least records it; and change the stdout line from an instruction to the user into an honest 'not read by the binary — run /batten-init to mine it'. Long term: hand `from` to the /batten-init skill through --scan-json (add a `from_doc` field to the scan facts).

findings.title: A one-character typo in a top-level spec key is silently ignored — `enforcment: report` makes doctor report `gates block`
findings.command: cd <sandbox>/run-init/typotest && sed -i 's/^enforcement: report/enforcment: report/' batten.yaml && export BATTEN_DB=<sandbox>/run-init/state.db && <testbed>/batten.exe doctor
findings.observed:
$ grep -n '^enforcment' batten.yaml
14:enforcment: report
$ batten.exe doctor | grep -i enforcement
✓ enforcement: enforce — gates block

And with the key spelled correctly:
● enforcement: REPORT — gates WARN, they do not block yet.

The same silence applies to any unknown key. I appended `bogus_top_level_key: 42` and got `✓ ...batten.yaml — project "branchtest", unit "US", 3 phases, 4 domains`, EXIT=0, no warning. The runtime loader agrees: `batten phase US-015 build` with the bogus key present ran fine (`anchor: US-015 base SHA = 44630cd`).
findings.expected: batten.schema.json declares `"additionalProperties": false` at the root (line 12). `batten doctor` — whose one-line description is 'validate spec, report live capabilities' — should reject or at least warn: `⚠ unknown key "enforcment" at top level (did you mean "enforcement"?)`.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the safety-critical key. A team that types `enforcment: report` believes gates warn; batten silently applies the default, which is `enforce`, and `git commit` starts getting denied for want of a verdict with nothing in the spec explaining why. The reverse typo pattern applies to `invariants`/`invariant` and `domains`/`domain`, where the failure is open instead of closed: the rules that 'ride VERBATIM into every fanned-out agent's prompt' just vanish, and neither doctor nor the loader says a word. doctor validates skill names and agent names against reality but not the spec's own key set against its own shipped schema.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a yaml.Decoder with KnownFields(true) so unknown keys are a load error, or validate the parsed document against the embedded batten.schema.json inside `doctor`. If a hard error is too aggressive for existing specs, emit `⚠ unknown key` per offender in doctor and keep Load permissive.

  frontend:

The two-letter domain names match inside unrelated words. `batten-engine`'s description contains 'batten.yaml' -> 'ya[ml]'; `ui-ux-pro-max`'s contains 'HTML/CSS' -> 'HT[ML]'; `portal-auth-jwt` has no 'db' anywhere except 'OAuth2Passwor[dB]earer' (grep -oin 'db' returns only `3:dB 39:dB 48:dB`, all inside PasswordBearer). findings.why_it_matters: batten.schema.json says of `skills`: these are what the domain's agent loads. A wrong entry spends fan-out context arguing for the wrong tool — an ML subagent told to load a UI/UX design skill and batten's own workflow engine. The prebuilt testbed binary (built 2026-07-27 23:52) predates internal/scan/scan.go (written 2026-07-28 00:06). Action needed: rebuild the testbed binary. Note the fix leaves portal-echarts-dashboards and portal-sse-streaming unmapped, which the new comment accepts as the deliberate trade ('Suggesting nothing is better').

findings.title: unit came out `TASK-\d+` and no `unit.plan`/`unit.locator`, in a repo whose backlog init itself catalogued
findings.command: cd <sandbox>/run-init/proyecto_ui && export BATTEN_DB=<sandbox>/run-init/state.db && <testbed>/batten.exe init --scan-json | head -5 && <testbed>/batten.exe init && sed -n '16,22p' batten.yaml
findings.observed:
scan.json:
  "unit_pattern": "TASK-\\d+",
  "unit_name": "TASK",
  "purpose": [ "context/planeacion_proyecto.md" ],
  notes: "no work-item pattern found in branch names; defaulted to TASK-N — edit unit.pattern to match your tracker (e.g. US-\\d{3}, PROJ-\\d+)"

batten.yaml:
unit:
  name: TASK
  pattern: 'TASK-\d+'

artifacts:
  handoff: docs/{id}.md   # TODO: where should per-unit handoffs live?

The file it names in purpose[] has 44 headings of the form `### US-001 — Entorno Docker Compose Multiservicio y Monorepo` (grep -c '^### US-' = 44). Nothing reads it: no `plan:` and no `locator:` key is emitted, although batten.schema.json defines both and its `locator` example is literally "'### {id}' finds the Markdown heading for US-034". The repo's root AGENTS.md states 'context/planeacion_proyecto.md — única fuente de verdad de las User Stories', and .claude/skills/portal-git-workflow/SKILL.md documents the branch shape 'feature/E{epic}-US-XXX-{slug}'.
findings.expected: `unit: {name: US, pattern: 'US-\d{3}', plan: context/planeacion_proyecto.md, locator: '### {id}'}` — every one of those four values is recoverable from a file the scan already opened.
findings.why_it_matters: unit.pattern is how batten answers 'which unit is this commit for?'. With TASK-\d+ against a US-### backlog, no branch, prompt or commit in this repo will ever match, so the anchor, the diff scoping and the verdict gate never bind to anything — the spec is inert on arrival. And `artifacts.handoff: docs/{id}.md` is a guess made in the same breath as ignoring the real plan doc, so a user who fixes only the pattern still has no route from a unit id to its acceptance criteria. Confirmed the inference machinery is fine, only its input source is: in a copy with `git checkout -b feature/E2-US-015-auth-jwt`, init emitted `unit="US"` / `pattern: 'US-\d{3}'`.
findings.suggested_fix: ALREADY FIXED AT HEAD — commit 3122d29 'fix: init reads the backlog for the unit, not just branch names' adds unitFromDocs()/pickUnit() and emits `plan:` and `locator:` (scan.go ~583-590). The testbed binary predates it; rebuild. When re-testing, check the US-UX-01..08 headings: pickUnit's regex reads those as prefix 'UX', so 'US' wins on count and the emitted `US-\d{3}` cannot match `US-UX-01` — 8 of 44 backlog items would stay invisible.

findings.title: The 9 custom subagents are discovered but never wired to a domain, and doctor cannot flag the omission
findings.command: cd <sandbox>/run-init/proyecto_ui && <testbed>/batten.exe init --scan-json | grep -c '"Source": "project"' && grep -c 'agent:' batten.yaml
findings.observed: scan.json's agents[] lists all 9 with descriptions — backend-engineer ('Specialist in FastAPI backend...'), frontend-engineer ('Specialist in Nuxt 4 frontend...'), data-engineer, agent-engineer, platform-engineer, security-reviewer, finops-auditor, ux-researcher, deliverable-writer. The generated batten.yaml contains zero `agent:` keys; `grep -n 'agent:' internal/scan/scan.go` at HEAD returns nothing, so ToYAML never emits one.
findings.expected: At minimum `domains.backend.agent: backend-engineer` and `domains.frontend.agent: frontend-engineer` — the two cases where the agent name is the domain name plus '-engineer' — or a note[] saying '9 custom agents found but not assigned; set domains.<d>.agent'.
findings.why_it_matters: batten.schema.json says of `agent`: 'The fan-out orchestrator uses it as the subagent type, so the DAG, the canvas and the hook matchers all show YOUR agent's name.' Without it the whole point of the run graph on a repo that already invested in 9 tuned agents — seeing your own agents in the DAG — is lost, and nothing in the draft or in doctor tells the user the key exists. This is arguably by design (the /batten-init skill is meant to supply the judgment from scan.json), but the binary-only path is the one users hit first and it produces a spec that silently ignores the repo's agents.
findings.file_hint: internal/scan/scan.go (Facts.ToYAML — Agents is populated but never rendered)
findings.suggested_fix: Emit `agent:` when a discovered agent's name starts with the domain name (backend-engineer -> backend), otherwise add a note[] listing the unassigned agents so the user knows the key exists.

findings.title: `batten doctor` validates a domain's rules file, skills and agent, but never that its `path` exists
findings.command: cd <sandbox>/run-init/branchtest && sed -i 's|    path: backend/|    path: does-not-exist/|; s|    rules: backend/AGENTS.md|    rules: nope/AGENTS.md|' batten.yaml && export BATTEN_DB=<sandbox>/run-init/state.db && <testbed>/batten.exe doctor
findings.observed:
✓ ...\branchtest\batten.yaml — project "branchtest", unit "US", 3 phases, 4 domains
✓ close gate: phase "close" requires verdict "ok" on any gate
⚠ gate "qa" declares no checks — it verifies NOTHING and approves on the agent's word.
● enforcement: REPORT — gates WARN, they do not block yet.
✓ store: ...\run-init\state.db
✓ graph: graphify (on PATH)
· memory: engram (via MCP; batten does not store episodic memory)
⚠ domain "backend": rules file missing: nope/AGENTS.md
EXIT=0

The bad rules path is reported. The bad `path: does-not-exist/` is not mentioned at all, and the header still says '4 domains'.
findings.expected: `⚠ domain "backend": path does not exist: does-not-exist/` alongside the rules warning — the same class of check, one line away in the same loop.
findings.why_it_matters: `path` is the fan-out axis and the write-set boundary. A domain pointing at a directory that does not exist (renamed dir, typo, monorepo reshuffle) means a subagent is fenced to nothing and the verify phase diffs nothing — and it fails silently mid-run, which is exactly the failure mode the schema says doctor exists to prevent ('a renamed skill should be caught there, not fail silently in the middle of an overnight run'). The rules/skills/agent checks prove the pattern is already there.
findings.file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go (doctor's domain loop, near line 1292 `⚠ domain %q: rules file missing`)
findings.suggested_fix: Add an os.Stat on filepath.Join(spec.Root, d.Path) in the same loop and warn when it is missing or not a directory.

findings.title: init says 'the stack is unknown' and 'NO check command was found' about a repo whose AGENTS.md — which init lists in harness[] — declares the stack and the exact QA gate commands
findings.command: cd <sandbox>/run-init/proyecto_ui && <testbed>/batten.exe init --scan-json | tail -12 && head -40 AGENTS.md
findings.observed:
scan.json:
  "stack": null,
  notes: "NO check command was found — gates.qa.checks is empty, which means the gate currently verifies nothing."
  notes: "no language marker files found; the stack is unknown and every check will need to be written by hand"
  harness: [ {"path": "AGENTS.md", "kind": "agent-rules", ...}, ... ]

AGENTS.md, the first file in that harness[] array, contains:
  ## Comandos
    make check            # lint + secrets-scan (OBLIGATORIO antes de PR)
    make lint             # ruff + mypy + pnpm lint (eslint)
    make test             # pytest backend/ml + vitest/Vue Test Utils frontend
  ## Stack — Decisiones Irrevocables  (a 14-row table: FastAPI/Polars, Nuxt 4, PostgreSQL 15 + pgvector, dbmate, ...)
  ## QA Gate antes de PR
    1. `make check` limpio (lint + secrets-scan).
    2. Tests cobertura >=70 % backend, >=50 % frontend.
findings.expected: The two notes should be scoped to what was actually searched — e.g. 'no build files (Makefile/pyproject.toml/package.json) found, so no check could be auto-detected; AGENTS.md documents commands (`make check`) — confirm they exist before filling gates.qa.checks'. As written they read as a claim about the repo, and they are false about the repo.
findings.why_it_matters: The scan opens the file, lists it in harness[], and puts 'the spec must agree with it, not replace it' at the top of the generated yaml — then reports the opposite of what that file says about the two most consequential empty fields (gates.qa.checks and the stack). A user reading only the notes concludes batten looked at their harness and found nothing there. It also makes `coverage: 70` / `coverage: 50` (a real schema key, stated verbatim in the QA Gate section) look undiscoverable. The warning itself is honest and correct in substance — the replica genuinely has no Makefile — so this is phrasing, not a wrong gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the evidence in the note: say which build files were looked for and not found, and cross-reference the harness files as the place to mine the commands from. Optionally have --scan-json return the `## Comandos`/`## QA Gate` blocks verbatim as a `harness_hints` field so /batten-init has something to reconcile against.

findings.title: `artifacts.handoff` is written into every spec but no phase reads it
findings.command: cd <sandbox>/run-init/proyecto_ui && sed -n '20,32p' batten.yaml
findings.observed:
artifacts:
  handoff: docs/{id}.md   # TODO: where should per-unit handoffs live?

phases:
  - id: build
    fanout: true
    anchor: git_sha
  - id: verify
    gate: qa
    diff_from: anchor
  - id: close

No phase carries a `reads:` key, so nothing references `handoff`. doctor reports `✓ ... 3 phases, 4 domains` with no comment.

summary: I copied the template repo to run-ws/proyecto_ui, wrote a batten.yaml with `fanout: true` on the build phase and the four domains (backend/frontend/ml/db), pointed BATTEN_DB at run-ws/state.db, and drove the guard entirely with real `batten phase` / `batten claim` / `batten hook SubagentStart` / `batten hook PreToolUse` invocations against hand-built payloads. All seven propositions in the brief hold: the second claim on a file is refused naming the owner; an attributed cross-agent Edit is denied naming the file, the owner, the trespasser's node and its own write-set; the owner writes silently; the same edit with no agent_id warns and never denies; an unclaimed file passes; a second open unit's session is denied with the OTHER unit named; and closing run A frees its files. The colliding claim is also fully atomic — a claim list containing one collision leaves nothing behind. Path handling is better than I expected: Windows case-folding, `../` traversal and native backslash paths all resolve to the claimed path and are denied. Session↔run binding is genuinely good (sess-A→US-001, sess-B→US-002, and an unbound third session gets a loud, honest "the gates can't act" warning rather than a silent no-op). The failures are all at the edges of that core, and two of them are serious: `batten claim` checks disjointness only WITHIN a run, so two open sessions can both be told they own the same file and then BOTH get denied on it — a mutual deadlock out of the exact multi-session scenario the guard advertises; and the `batten_writeset_owner` MCP tool that the plugin explicitly tells fanned-out subagents to call before writing reports `write_allowed: true` for files the hook denies a second later. Beyond that: NotebookEdit is wired into the guard but reads the wrong JSON key so it is never guarded; a denied Edit can be redone verbatim through Bash with no warning; and opening a second unit silently steals the first unit's phase node, emptying its DAG and its exported canvas.
worked: (1) Second claim on the same file is refused and names the owner. `batten claim agent-frontend-1 <repo>/backend/app/main.py` after agent-backend-1 owned it → `batten: write-set collision: backend/app/main.py is already owned by n-agent-backend-1`, rc=1.

(Bonus) The claim is ATOMIC. `batten claim agent-frontend-1 frontend/pages/index.vue backend/app/main.py frontend/pages/other.vue` (collision in the middle) → same collision error, rc=1, and `batten show US-001` afterwards showed frontend with NO `owns N file(s)` at all. Confirmed independently: a PreToolUse from a different agent on frontend/pages/index.vue was allowed (empty output), proving the first path in the list was not left claimed. `defer tx.Rollback()` in ClaimWriteSet does its job.

(2) Attributed trespass is DENIED with everything a fix needs. PreToolUse {tool_name:Edit, agent_id:agent-frontend-1, file_path:<repo>/backend/app/main.py} → permissionDecision `deny`, reason names the file (backend/app/main.py), the owner (n-agent-backend-1), the trespasser (n-agent-frontend-1) AND B's own write-set listed line by line (frontend/pages/index.vue, frontend/pages/other.vue), plus 'fix the plan, do not cross the fence'.

(3) The owner writing its own claimed file is allowed silently — empty stdout, rc=0, for both `Edit` (backend/app/main.py) and `Write` (backend/app/routers.py). Re-verified while a second unit was open, so the cross-run check does not false-positive on the legitimate owner.

(4) The same edit with NO agent_id WARNS and never denies, exactly as hooks.go documents: `{"systemMessage":"batten (warning — not blocking): batten: backend/app/main.py is claimed by a fanned-out agent (n-agent-backend-1) in this run..."}` with no permissionDecision field. An agent_id that is present but unknown to the store falls into the same advisory path — the fail-open is on the unattributable case, not on the absent-field case only.
(5) A file nobody claimed is allowed silently: PreToolUse Write on ml/pipelines/eda.py with agent_id agent-backend-1 → empty output, rc=0.

(6) Cross-session denial names the OTHER unit. With US-001 (sess-A) and US-002 (sess-B) both open, sess-B editing backend/app/main.py → `deny`: 'backend/app/main.py is being worked by US-001 in another open session (run US-001-1785219540528530400-5c67d782). Editing it now races that work. Coordinate, or use a worktree per unit.' Symmetric in the other direction (sess-A denied on db/migrations/0001.sql, named US-002), and an UNBOUND third session (sess-C) is fenced too.

(7) Closing run A releases its claims, on both paths. `batten close US-001 --status rolled_back` → 'US-001 closed (rolled_back). Write-set claims released — files it held are free again.' and sess-B's previously-denied Edit then returned empty (allowed). Happy path likewise: `batten check US-004` → '✓ echo qa-ok / US-004: OK (batten-verified)', then `batten close US-004` → closed ok, and the file it held became writable by the other session.

Closing as ok is itself gated: `batten close US-001` with no verdict → 'batten: cannot close US-001 as ok: needs a verdict with result=ok and cited evidence (run `batten check US-001`, or the verify phase). Use --status failed to close a run that went wrong', rc=1. A failed/rolled_back close is always available, so claims can never get permanently stuck behind the verdict gate.

Session↔run binding is decisive and honest. SessionStart for sess-A → '→ this session is working **US-001**.'; sess-B → '**US-002**'; a third, unbound session → '⚠ 2 units are open (US-001, US-002) and this session isn't bound to one. The gates can't act until you bind it...'. Branch-based binding also works: after `git checkout -b feature/US-003-algo`, a brand-new session resolved to US-003 with no prior state. `AdoptSession` only fills an empty session_id, so one session cannot steal another's run.

Path normalization is solid on Windows. Against a claim of ml/pipelines/eda.py, all three of `<repo>/ML/PIPELINES/EDA.PY` (case-folded), `<repo>/backend/../ml/pipelines/eda.py` (traversal) and the native backslash form `C:\...\proyecto_ui\ml\pipelines\eda.py` were DENIED. No trivial spelling escape from the fence.

batten hook SubagentStart <<< '{"session_id":"s1","cwd":"<repo>","agent_id":"A1","agent_type":"backend"}'

batten phase US-011 build
batten hook SubagentStart <<< '{"session_id":"s2","cwd":"<repo>","agent_id":"B1","agent_type":"backend"}'
batten claim B1 <repo>/backend/app/main.py
batten hook PreToolUse <<< '{"cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Edit","agent_id":"A1","tool_input":{"file_path":"<repo>/backend/app/main.py"}}'
batten hook PreToolUse <<< '{"cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Edit","agent_id":"B1","tool_input":{"file_path":"<repo>/backend/app/main.py"}}'
findings.observed:
-- B1 (run US-011) claims the file A1 (run US-010) already owns:
B1 owns 1 file(s); any other agent writing them is now denied
rc=0
-- A1 (a declared owner) edits it:
DENY: batten: backend/app/main.py is being worked by US-011 in another open session (run US-011-1785220325904134100-97b4d3ac).
-- B1 (a declared owner) edits it:
DENY: batten: backend/app/main.py is being worked by US-010 in another open session (run US-010-1785220305472668900-06c198dc).
findings.expected: The second `batten claim` should fail the same way an in-run collision does — `write-set collision: backend/app/main.py is already owned by US-010 (run ...)`, rc=1 — so the planning bug surfaces at claim time, where the build skill says to fix the plan. Instead the collision is accepted with a reassuring message and detonates later as a mutual deadlock in which neither declared owner can write the file it was told it owns, and neither denial message mentions that the caller is itself a recorded owner.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the exact scenario the write-set guard exists for, and it is the one ROADMAP.md line 35 claims is 'enforced by a PRIMARY KEY (run_id, path), so disjointness is a database constraint, not advice' and line 38 claims is 'write-sets defended between open runs'. The PK is per-run, so across runs disjointness is neither a constraint nor advice — it is nothing at claim time, and a hard deadlock at write time. Two parallel sessions (the documented multi-session workflow) plus one overlapping file bricks both fan-outs at hour six of an unattended run, and the escape hatch is non-obvious: nothing in the deny message tells you a duplicate claim was recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: In ClaimWriteSet, before inserting, also run the WriteSetOwnerAcrossOpenRuns check that the hook already uses, and refuse with the owning unit and run named. That makes the claim command agree with the guard, and turns the deadlock into a plan bug caught at claim time.

findings.title: The `batten_writeset_owner` MCP tool reports `write_allowed: true` for files the PreToolUse guard denies
findings.expected: The advisory tool must never be more permissive than the gate. Case A: `agent_id` was supplied and `NodeByAgent` resolves that agent's run unambiguously, so resolveRun should use it instead of declaring 'no active run … nothing is enforced'. Case B: the tool should run the same WriteSetOwnerAcrossOpenRuns check the hook runs, and return `write_allowed: false` naming US-004. When the run genuinely cannot be resolved, the honest default is `write_allowed: null`/unknown with the reason — not `true`.
findings.why_it_matters: The MCP server's own instructions say 'Before writing a file as a fanned-out subagent call batten_writeset_owner', and the tool description says 'if another agent owns it, the PreToolUse hook will DENY your Write/Edit'. In a multi-session repo the tool tells the agent the opposite of what the hook will do, so the agent burns a turn on a write that gets denied — and worse, the note 'nothing is enforced' actively teaches the agent that the fence is off. It is also the one place batten breaks its own stated principle of never reporting an unmeasurable thing permissively.
findings.suggested_fix: In writeSetOwner: (1) if AgentID resolves a node, use that node's RunID as the run rather than falling through to resolveRun's ambiguity path; (2) after the in-run WriteSetOwner check, call st.WriteSetOwnerAcrossOpenRuns(project, rel, run.RunID) and set write_allowed=false with the other unit named; (3) initialise WriteAllowed only after a run is resolved, so the unresolved case cannot default to true.

findings.title: Opening a second unit steals the first unit's phase node, emptying its run DAG and its exported canvas
findings.command:
export BATTEN_DB=.../run-ws/state.db
batten phase US-012 build
batten hook SubagentStart <<< '{"session_id":"s3","cwd":"<repo>","agent_id":"C1","agent_type":"backend"}'
batten show US-012 ; batten canvas US-012 --out us012-before.canvas
batten phase US-013 build          # a second session opens another unit
batten show US-012 ; batten canvas US-012 --out us012-after.canvas
findings.observed:
=== BEFORE — US-012's DAG:
US-012  run=US-012-1785220349240324700-346df4be  status=running  phase=build  base=44630cd
  [phase] build                    running 
  [subagent] backend                  running 
wrote .../us012-before.canvas (4 nodes, 1 edges)

=== a second session opens ANOTHER unit: batten phase US-013 build

=== AFTER — US-012's DAG:
US-012  run=US-012-1785220349240324700-346df4be  status=running  phase=build  base=44630cd
  [subagent] backend                  running 
wrote .../us012-after.canvas (1 nodes, 0 edges)
findings.expected: US-012's DAG should be unaffected by anything US-013 does. Node ids must be namespaced per run. `AddNode` does `INSERT OR REPLACE` on a globally-unique `node_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, and `cmdPhase` builds that id as `"p-" + phaseID` with no run in it — so every `batten phase <any-unit> build` in a shared DB moves the single row `p-build` to the newest run. The effect ping-pongs: re-running `batten phase US-002 build` moved the node back to US-002 (canvas 1→4 nodes) and simultaneously emptied US-003 (4→1). It also survived a run being closed: US-001, closed and rolled_back, still exported an empty canvas.
findings.why_it_matters: The canvas/vault export is the human-facing artifact of a run, and it goes from 4 nodes to just a header the moment a colleague (or the same user in a second terminal) starts another unit — silently, with no error. canvas.Render has an explicit 'orphans get their own column so nothing is silently dropped' safety net, but it only catches nodes with NO parent edge; here the subagents still have a `spawn` edge pointing at a `p-build` node that now belongs to a different run, so they are dropped anyway. `batten show` degrades the same way, losing the phase row. Everything downstream that reasons over the DAG (canvas, vault note, TUI) inherits it.
findings.file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go (cmdPhase, `NodeID: "p-" + phaseID` ~line 368) and internal/store/store.go (AddNode INSERT OR REPLACE ~line 404)
findings.suggested_fix: Make the phase node id run-scoped — `"p-" + run.RunID + "-" + phaseID` (hooks.go's `AddEdge(run.RunID, "p-"+run.Phase, ...)` and any other constructor must use the same helper). Belt and braces: have canvas.Render treat a child whose parent node is absent from `nodes` as an orphan rather than dropping it, so a stale edge can never make work disappear.

batten hook PreToolUse <<< '{"session_id":"s1","cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Edit","agent_id":"A2","tool_input":{"file_path":"<repo>/backend/app/main.py"}}'
batten hook PreToolUse <<< '{"session_id":"s1","cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Bash","agent_id":"A2","tool_input":{"command":"python - <<PY\nopen('backend/app/main.py','w').write('# rewritten by A2\\n')\nPY"}}'

-- A2 Edit on A1's file:
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"batten: write-set collision. backend/app/main.py belongs to another agent's write-set (n-A1); you are n-A2...."}}

-- A2 does the IDENTICAL write via Bash:
[]  <- empty = allowed, no warning
findings.expected: At minimum a visible warning on the Bash path, in the spirit of the project's own principle #3 ('fail open only with a warning'). PreToolUse already fires on Bash for the verdict gate (plugin/claude-code/hooks/hooks.json matches Bash), so the payload reaches the binary — batten simply never looks at the command for writes into claimed paths. A cheap heuristic (shell redirects `>`/`>>`/`tee`, plus `sed -i`, `mv`, `cp`, `patch`, `python ... open(...,'w')`) covering the obvious cases would turn a silent bypass into a loud one.
findings.why_it_matters: The write-set guard is the project's headline claim ('Two agents must never write the same file — that is what makes the fan-out safe'), and the deny message tells the agent to fix the plan rather than route around the fence. A model that has just been denied will very plausibly reach for Bash — this is the single most likely real-world escape, it leaves no trace, and no doc I could find (README.md, DESIGN.md, ROADMAP.md, batten-build.md) states that the guard covers only Write/Edit/NotebookEdit. Users will read 'denied by a hook' as 'cannot happen'.

findings.suggested_fix: In the Bash branch, after verdictGate, scan the command for repo-relative/absolute paths that appear as write targets and run them through the same ownership lookup; emit `advise()` (never deny — a false positive on a shell string must not block a session) naming the file and its owner. findings.title: A directory claim is accepted and reported as protecting files, but fences nothing
findings.command:
batten claim agent-fe-4 <repo>/frontend/
batten hook PreToolUse <<< '{"session_id":"sess-E","cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Edit","agent_id":"agent-be-4","tool_input":{"file_path":"<repo>/frontend/pages/index.vue"}}'
findings.observed:
agent-fe-4 owns 1 file(s); any other agent writing them is now denied
rc=0
--- other agent edits a file UNDER the claimed directory
ALLOWED (empty)
findings.expected: Either reject a claim on an existing directory ('a write-set is a list of files; frontend/ is a directory — list the files, or claim frontend/** if prefix claims are supported'), or honour it as a prefix claim and deny writes underneath. What must not happen is the current outcome: the command asserts 'any other agent writing them is now denied' about a claim that denies nothing. Related and equally silent: `batten claim agent-fe-4 C:/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts` (outside the repo) was also accepted with 'owns 1 file(s)', and can never match, because cmdClaim keeps the absolute path when filepath.Rel escapes the root while writeSetGuard only ever computes repo-relative paths.
findings.why_it_matters: 'This agent owns frontend/' is the most natural way for a planner to express a write-set, and batten's own plan/build skills describe write-sets in per-domain terms ('domain <D> — 4 agents'). The orchestrator gets an unqualified success message and a false sense of protection, and the failure is invisible until two agents have already written the same file — which is precisely the outcome the guard is sold on preventing. A claim that silently protects nothing is worse than a rejected claim.
findings.suggested_fix: In cmdClaim, `os.Stat` each argument: reject directories with a message that shows the file-list form, and reject (or at least warn on) paths whose relative form starts with `..`. Print the claimed paths back, not just a count, so 'owns 1 file(s)' can never hide a claim on the wrong thing.

dimension: THE VERDICT GATE — batten's core promise
summary: I built an isolated sandbox at .../scratchpad/batten-testbed/run-gate/proyecto_ui (copy of the replica repo, BATTEN_DB pointed at run-gate/state.db, no remote, real batten.exe), hand-wrote a batten.yaml with unit pattern 'US-\d{3}', a qa gate carrying two REAL checks (`python -m pytest backend/tests -q`, `python -m compileall -q backend`) with verdict+evidence required, a close phase with requires_verdict: ok, and enforcement: enforce. I added a real Python module and a real 3-test pytest suite so the checks had something true to say, then drove `batten hook PreToolUse` directly with the payload shape from internal/hooks/hooks.go across ~40 scenarios and 6 units (US-011..US-016) and 6 sessions. Verdict: the gate's substance is real and holds up under adversarial pressure — all seven requested behaviours reproduced as promised. An empty evidence[] is refused by the binary (exit 1); a blocked verdict denies with why+safe_next_step; `batten check` genuinely runs the declared commands in the repo root, records source=batten, and a real pytest failure produces BLOCKED citing the real output; an agent-written ok is NOT enough when checks are declared; an agent cannot forge source=batten (the field is json:"-") nor talk past a batten BLOCKED by writing ok on top; override works and demands a reason; report mode turns every violation into a warning. What is weak is not the logic but its perimeter and its aftermath. Three ordinary ways of spelling a commit — `git -C . commit`, `git -c user.email=x commit`, `git.exe commit` — walk straight through the gate, silently. A unit whose run was never opened with `batten phase` is not gated at all, with zero output. `batten check` alone (which knows nothing about the unit) is sufficient to close a unit with an empty diff and no acceptance-criteria judgment. And once you override, no CLI surface shows it — `batten show` actively says the gate will deny while the hook allows.
worked: 1. Commit with NO verdict is denied, actionably. `batten phase US-011 build` then the PreToolUse hook returned: {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"batten: US-011 has no verdict envelope. Run the \"verify\" phase before committing.\nTo proceed anyway (recorded in the audit log): batten override US-011 --reason \"...\""}} — names the unit, names the phase to run, and offers the audited escape.

2. `batten verdict` with result ok and empty evidence[] is refused by the binary, exit 1. Both `"evidence":[]` and the evidence key omitted entirely produced: `batten: result "ok" with an empty evidence[] is not allowed: an approval must cite something (command output, test counts, a criterion verified). Without evidence the result is "blocked"` with [exit=1]. Nothing reached the database.

AC3 is unimplemented: rejected grains are not written to the audit log\nsafe_next_step: implement the audit-log write in resolve_grain, add a test for it, then re-run the verify phase\nTo proceed anyway (recorded): batten override US-011 --reason \"...\"". `batten verdict` also warned at record time: "the close gate will deny a commit while this stands at \"blocked\"".

A failing check produced blocked, never a pass. Restoring the guard flipped it to "US-011: OK (batten-verified). all gate checks passed (batten ran them)".

5. source=batten is really recorded. sqlite on the sandbox DB: (4, 'qa', 'US-011-qa-batten', 'blocked', 'batten', '["python -m pytest backend/tests -q: FAIL (exit 1)\\n ... raise AssertionError...') alongside the agent rows (1..3, source 'agent'). `batten runs` distinguishes them with a footnote: "* batten-verified: the gate's checks were actually run".

(b) Writing an ok verdict ON TOP of a batten-produced blocked did NOT open the gate — LatestVerdictBySource(batten) still governs. Both reproduced.

8. `batten override` opens the gate and demands a reason. `batten override US-014` -> "batten: --reason is required: an override with no stated reason is just a disabled gate" [exit=1]; whitespace-only --reason "   " refused identically; with a real reason it printed "override recorded for US-014 (gate qa): ..." and the next PreToolUse returned empty output (ALLOW). The row is in the overrides table: (1, 'US-014-...', 'qa', 'hotfix for the Friday demo; QA runs Monday, tracked in US-014-followup', 1785219898).

All three (no verdict / blocked verdict / checks-not-run) returned a systemMessage "batten (warning — not blocking): ..." plus the full reason in additionalContext, and NO permissionDecision field — e.g. {"systemMessage":"batten (warning — not blocking): batten: US-015 verdict is "blocked", not "ok". reconnect loses events","hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","additionalContext":"batten warning:
...
safe_next_step: buffer the last event id before reconnecting
..."}}. Flipping back to enforce restored the denials.

10. The documented fail-open path behaves as documented, loudly. With gates.qa.checks removed, `batten doctor` said: ⚠ gate "qa" declares no checks — it verifies NOTHING and approves on the agent's word. Add gates.qa.checks ... and the hook — even under enforcement: enforce — emitted a warning rather than a denial: "batten: gate \"qa\" declares no checks, so US-016 was approved on the agent's word alone — nothing was run to verify it."

Sitting on branch feature/US-015-sse-streaming, session s1 (adopted onto US-011 earlier) was gated on US-011 ("batten: US-011 verdict is \"blocked\"...") while session s5 on the same branch was gated on US-015 — two sessions, two units, correctly separated.
12. Checks execute in the repo root, not the process cwd. A probe check printed: CWD: $HOME\AppData\Local\Temp\...\run-gate\proyecto_ui.

13. End-to-end works. `batten phase US-011 close` -> hook allows (batten ok on record) -> real `git commit` succeeds (4642a9a) -> PostToolUse closed the run: `batten runs` shows US-011 / ok / close / ok*.

Compound and prefixed commit forms are caught: `cd backend && git commit -m x`, `git   commit -m x` (extra spaces), `git commit --amend --no-edit`, `git --no-pager commit -m x`, `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=x git commit -m y`, and `git status; git commit -m x` all returned deny. `git push origin HEAD` correctly returned no opinion.

findings.title: Three ordinary spellings of `git commit` walk straight through the verdict gate
findings.command: cd <repo> && printf '{"session_id":"s5","cwd":"<repo>","hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git -c user.email=a@b.c commit -m x"}}' | batten.exe hook PreToolUse
findings.observed:
=== A: plain form (US-015, session s5) ===
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"batten: US-015 has no batten-verified pass. The gate's checks must be RUN, not asserted.\nRun: batten check US-015\nTo proceed anyway (recorded): batten override US-015 --reason \"...\""}}

=== B: same commit via git -C (the form used when not at the repo root) ===
<no output above == ALLOWED>

=== C: same commit via git -c user.email=... (the non-interactive form) ===
<no output above == ALLOWED>

=== D: same commit via git.exe ===
<no output above == ALLOWED>
findings.expected: All four spellings denied identically. `git -C <dir> commit`, `git -c user.email=... commit` and `git.exe commit` are the same act as `git commit`.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the one denial the product is built around, and the forms that escape it are not exotic: `git -c user.name=... -c user.email=... commit` is the standard non-interactive commit an agent or CI emits (it is what I myself typed to make the sandbox's baseline commit, before I noticed), and `git -C <dir> commit` is what you write the moment you are not at the repo root. `commitRe = (^|[;&|]|\s)git\s+(-[^\s]+\s+)*commit\b` consumes flags but not the separate ARGUMENT git's global flags take, so `-C .` and `-c k=v` break the match. The `.exe` miss is an internal inconsistency: the file's own phaseRe already writes `batten(?:\.exe)?`, so the author knew the form and forgot it 70 lines later — on Windows, batten's stated primary platform.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the program, then scan the rest of the argv for a bare `commit` token: e.g. `(^|[;&|]|\s)git(\.exe)?\s+(?:-[^\s]+(?:[=\s]\S+)?\s+)*commit\b`, and add table tests for `git -C . commit`, `git -c a=b commit`, `git.exe commit`, `git --git-dir=x commit`. Better still: since a missed commit is a silent hole in the core promise, bias to over-matching — treat any Bash command containing the token `commit` preceded by a `git`-ish program as a gate event, and let a false positive be a warning rather than let a real commit through unseen.

dimension: PHASES, ANCHOR, CLOSE, and the run record
summary: I copied the proyecto_ui replica to run-life/proyecto_ui, pointed BATTEN_DB at run-life/state.db, wrote a 6-phase batten.yaml (research/plan/build/verify/fix/close) with `anchor: git_sha` on build and `diff_from: anchor` on verify, and drove US-001 end to end: 5 real commits interleaved with `batten phase`, an agent verdict, `batten check`, `batten close`, then `batten runs` / `batten show` / `batten canvas`, plus a second unit, a second run of the same unit, three hook sessions, and a backdated DB to force the stale-run path. The core lifecycle mechanics hold up well: the anchor is stamped exactly once at the build phase and provably does not move across four later commits or across a re-entry into build; `batten close` releases the unit and the next `batten phase` opens a genuinely new run with a fresh run id, cleared anchor and cleared verdict; the close gate is per-run, so the reopened run could not ride the old run's verdict; `batten runs` shows verdict state including the `ok*` batten-verified footnote and `blocked`; and SessionStart reports unit ambiguity rather than guessing. But the *run record itself* is the weak part, and I found one clear data-loss bug: phase nodes are keyed globally by `p-<phase>`, so the moment a second unit enters a phase name the first unit's phase row is silently transplanted out of its run — `batten show US-001` loses its `plan` row because US-002 entered `plan`. Around that sit two gate inconsistencies (`batten close --status ok` accepts a verdict the commit hook refuses; the README's documented verdict→commit flow is denied in practice), a run record where every phase reads `running` forever including after close, a doctor stale-warning that no amount of activity can clear because `events.run_id` is always NULL, a commit gate that silently stops enforcing whenever 2+ unowned runs are open, and no validation of unit ids against the declared `unit.pattern` — which is how you get the extra open runs that disable the gate in the first place.
worked: ANCHOR IS RECORDED ONCE AND DOES NOT MOVE (claim 1, PROVEN). `batten phase US-001 build` at HEAD=7a332be printed `anchor: US-001 base SHA = 7a332be`. I then landed two real commits (4ff18eb, 11aafe9) and `batten show US-001` still read `base=7a332be`. Two more commits (9dfda3e, 70a7179) later: still `base=7a332be`. Re-entering the anchor phase (`batten phase US-001 build` a second time, with HEAD now 11aafe9) also left it at `base=7a332be` — the anchor is genuinely stamped once per run, guarded by `if ph.Anchor == "git_sha" && run.BaseSHA == ""` (cmd/batten/main.go:372).

SHOW REPORTS THE RIGHT RUN AFTER CLOSE (claim 2, PROVEN under normal clocks). After `batten close US-001`: `US-001  run=US-001-1785219518711611100-3feffc7f  status=ok  phase=close  base=7a332be`. After reopening with `batten phase US-001 plan`: `US-001  run=US-001-1785219778305899600-93c6291a  status=running  phase=plan  base=` — the new run, not the old one. Selection is `ORDER BY started_at DESC, rowid DESC` (internal/store/store.go:329), with the rowid tiebreak so a coarse clock does not make it a coin flip.

RUNS LISTS UNITS WITH VERDICT STATE (claim 3, PROVEN). `batten runs` rendered all four states across my runs: `—` (no verdict), `ok` (agent verdict), `ok*` with the footnote `* batten-verified: the gate's checks were actually run`, and `blocked`. Full example: `US-006  running  build   —` / `US-005  failed   verify  blocked` / `US-001  ok  close  ok*`.

CLOSE RELEASES THE UNIT AND THE NEXT PHASE OPENS A GENUINELY NEW RUN (claim 4, PROVEN). `batten close US-001` -> `US-001 closed (ok). Write-set claims released — files it held are free again.` Then `batten phase US-001 plan` minted run `US-001-1785219778305899600-93c6291a` (new id) with `base=` empty and no verdict. Both rows appear in `batten runs`. Critically the close gate is per-run, not per-unit: `batten close US-001` on the reopened run was refused — `batten: cannot close US-001 as ok: needs a verdict with result=ok and cited evidence (run `batten check US-001`, or the verify phase).` The old run's `ok` verdict did not leak forward. That is the right call and it is the single most important thing about run identity.

SESSION BINDING BINDS CORRECTLY AND REPORTS AMBIGUITY RATHER THAN GUESSING (claim 5, mostly PROVEN). With two open unowned runs, `hook SessionStart` for a fresh session returned: `⚠ 2 units are open (US-001, US-002) and this session isn't bound to one.\n   The gates can't act until you bind it: run `batten phase <unit> <phase>`.\n   For parallel work, a worktree per unit keeps each on its own branch.` — it refused to pick. Then `git checkout -b feature/US-002` and a PreToolUse from session sessB bound sessB to the US-002 run (DB: `('US-002-...','US-002','sessB','running')`) and denied the commit naming the correct unit: `batten: US-002 has no verdict envelope. Run the "verify" phase before committing.` Branch-name binding works, and it is decisive from then on (internal/hooks/hooks.go:626-666). The gap is what happens at PreToolUse *while* ambiguous — see finding on the silently disabled gate.

DOCTOR'S STALE-RUN WARNING DOES FIRE (claim 6, PROVEN — but see the finding on how it behaves). Backdating one open run's `started_at` by 100h made it fire: `⚠ 1 run(s) open >48h with no activity — close or resume them:\n    US-001 (phase plan): batten close US-001 [--status ok|failed]`, and restoring the timestamp made it go away.

THE EMPTY-EVIDENCE REJECTION IS REAL. `echo '{"check_id":"US-001-qa","result":"ok","evidence":[]}' | batten verdict --unit US-001` -> exit 1, `batten: result "ok" with an empty evidence[] is not allowed: an approval must cite something (command output, test counts, a criterion verified). Without evidence the result is "blocked"` — exactly as the README promises, character for character.

`batten check` GENUINELY RUNS THE GATE'S COMMANDS. With no Makefile: `✗ make check (exit 2) / make: *** No rule to make target 'check'.  Stop.` -> `US-001: BLOCKED (batten-verified)`. After adding a real Makefile: `✓ make check / ✓ make test / US-001: OK (batten-verified). all gate checks passed (batten ran them)`, recorded as evidence with real timings (`make check: PASS (exit 0, 146ms)`). This is the strongest thing in the tool — the mechanical half of the gate is true by construction, not by assertion.

BLOCKED VERDICTS HOLD THE CLOSE. `batten close US-005` with a `blocked` verdict -> exit 1 with the message above; `batten close US-005 --status failed` -> `US-005 closed (failed). Write-set claims released` and `batten runs` shows `US-005  failed  verify  blocked`. A run that went wrong is always closeable, which is right — otherwise its claims would be stuck forever.

SPEC VALIDATION AND DB ISOLATION ARE CLEAN. `batten phase US-001 deploy` -> exit 1, `batten: no phase "deploy" in batten.yaml`. `batten close US-777` -> exit 1, `batten: no open run for US-777`. `BATTEN_DB` was honored everywhere and `batten doctor` echoes it back: `✓ store: .../run-life/state.db` — the user's real ~/.batten/batten.db was never written.

findings.title: A second unit entering the same phase name silently steals the phase row out of the first unit's run record
findings.command:
export BATTEN_DB=.../run-life/minimal.db
batten phase US-001 plan && batten phase US-001 build && batten show US-001
batten phase US-002 plan
batten show US-001
findings.observed:
--- US-001: plan, build ---
US-001  run=US-001-1785220176474848000-800c8b9d  status=running  phase=build  base=70a7179
  [phase] plan                     running 
  [phase] build                    running 

--- now US-002 enters plan ---

--- show US-001 again (nothing else touched it) ---
US-001  run=US-001-1785220176474848000-800c8b9d  status=running  phase=build  base=70a7179
  [phase] build                    running
findings.expected: US-001's run record is immutable with respect to anything US-002 does. `batten show US-001` should still list both `plan` and `build`.
findings.why_it_matters: Two units open at once is the headline use case (the README's fan-out story, the multi-session row in ROADMAP.md). The cause is that phase nodes are keyed globally: `NodeID: "p-" + phaseID` (cmd/batten/main.go:368) against `node_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` with `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO nodes` (internal/store/store.go:404). The row is not duplicated, it is *transplanted* — its run_id is rewritten to the new run. I confirmed in SQLite that US-001's first run ended up with p-research/p-build/p-verify/p-close and no p-plan at all, and after `batten phase FOO-9 build` a still-open US-001 run in phase `build` had literally zero phase nodes, so `batten show US-001` printed a header and nothing else. `FinishNode` has the same bug (`UPDATE nodes SET status=? ... WHERE node_id=?`, store.go:413) — finishing a phase would finish whichever run currently owns that node id. This is silent, permanent corruption of the exact artifact this dimension is about, and it also poisons `batten canvas`, the TUI and the vault export, which all read the same nodes.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the nodes primary key composite: `PRIMARY KEY (run_id, node_id)`, and change FinishNode/AddEdge/lookups to key on (run_id, node_id). Alternatively prefix the node id with the run id. A migration is needed for existing DBs.

findings.title: `batten close --status ok` accepts an agent-asserted verdict that the commit gate refuses — the "checks must be RUN, not asserted" rule has a documented back door
findings.command:
export BATTEN_DB=.../run-life/minimal2.db
git checkout -b feature/US-001
batten phase US-001 build && batten phase US-001 verify
batten verdict --unit US-001 --file v2.json   # agent verdict, result ok, 3 evidence strings
batten phase US-001 close
printf '{"session_id":"s1","cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git commit -m \"feat(US-001): rate limiting\""}}' | batten hook PreToolUse
batten close US-001
findings.observed:
verdict recorded: US-001 qa=ok (3 evidence)
--- README says this commit now goes through ---
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"batten: US-001 has no batten-verified pass. The gate's checks must be RUN, not asserted.\nRun: batten check US-001\nTo proceed anyway (recorded): batten override US-001 --reason \"...\""}}
--- and batten close ---
US-001 closed (ok). Write-set claims released — files it held are free again.
EXIT=0
findings.expected: Both paths enforce the same rule. If the commit hook demands a verdict with `source='batten'` because the gate declares `checks`, then `batten close --status ok` must demand it too — or refuse and say so.
findings.why_it_matters: The two enforcement paths disagree, and the weaker one wins. The DB after this sequence reads `('US-001','ok','close','70a7179')` with a single verdict row of `('qa','ok','agent')` — the unit is recorded as cleanly closed, its write-set claims are released, and the resolution artifact is stamped, without `make check` or `make test` ever having been executed. The code even claims otherwise: cmd/batten/main.go:678 says "Closing as ok obeys the same rule as the commit gate", but `gateReadyToClose` (main.go:698-713) only calls `LatestVerdict` and never `LatestVerdictBySource(..., "batten")` the way internal/hooks/hooks.go:329 does. An agent that gets denied at the commit can close the run anyway and the run record will say it passed.
findings.suggested_fix: In `gateReadyToClose`, mirror the hook: when `sp.Gates[gate].Checks` is non-empty, require `LatestVerdictBySource(run.RunID, gate, "batten").Result == "ok"`. Better still, extract one `gateVerdictOK(spec, store, run)` helper and call it from both the hook and cmdClose so they cannot drift again.

findings.title: The README's headline flow is wrong: recording a verdict with cited evidence does NOT let the commit through
findings.command:
batten verdict --unit US-001 --file verdict.json   # result ok, 3 evidence items
printf '{"session_id":"s1","cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git commit -m \"feat(US-001): x\""}}' | batten hook PreToolUse
findings.observed:
verdict recorded: US-001 qa=ok (3 evidence)
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"batten: US-001 has no batten-verified pass. The gate's checks must be RUN, not asserted.\nRun: batten check US-001\nTo proceed anyway (recorded): batten override US-001 --reason \"...\""}}
findings.expected: README.md lines 58-66 state: "A verdict that cites three real things gets through, and only then: $ batten verdict --unit US-034 --file verdict.json / verdict US-034-qa: ok (3 evidence) / $ git commit -m ... / [feature/US-034 8f2a1c9] feat: add order rate limiting". Either the commit succeeds as documented, or the README documents the `batten check` step.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the product's central worked example and it does not reproduce. A first-time user follows the README exactly, produces a verdict with three genuine citations, and is still denied — by a message pointing at a command (`batten check`) that appears nowhere in the README, nowhere in `batten --help`, and nowhere in batten.schema.json. The new behaviour is *better* than the documented one, which makes it worse that it is undocumented: the user's reasonable conclusion is that the gate is broken. The same gap exists in plugin/claude-code/skills/batten-verdict/SKILL.md, which teaches the envelope and says nothing about `batten check`.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the README's worked example to `batten check US-034` -> `batten verdict ...` -> `git commit`, and say explicitly that a gate with declared `checks` requires a batten-produced verdict. Add the same note to the batten-verdict and batten-verify skills and to the `gates.checks` description in batten.schema.json.

findings.title: `batten check` and `batten close` exist but are absent from `batten --help` — including the command the deny message tells you to run
findings.command:
batten --help
batten --help | grep -i 'check\|close'
batten check US-001
batten close US-001
findings.observed:
batten --help lists exactly: init, doctor, hook, phase, claim, verdict, runs, show, canvas, budget, override, tui, mcp, statusline, ingest.

$ batten --help | grep -i 'check\|close'
(grep exit=1 — no matches)

$ batten check US-001
  ✓ make check
  ✓ make test
US-001: OK (batten-verified). all gate checks passed (batten ran them)

$ batten close US-001
US-001 closed (ok). Write-set claims released — files it held are free again.
findings.expected: Every dispatched subcommand appears in `--help`. `close` is the terminal step of the documented lifecycle and `check` is what every denial tells the user to run.
findings.why_it_matters: The gate denies a commit and says `Run: batten check US-001`. The user runs `batten --help` to find out what that is and it is not there; nor is it in README.md or batten.schema.json. `batten close` — the command that ends a run — is equally invisible. `measure`, `hook-debug` and `version` are also undispatched from help (cmd/batten/main.go:79-87). Compounding it, argument parsing silently swallows unknown flags: `batten runs --help` prints `no runs yet` instead of usage, and `batten show US-001 --json`, `--run <id>` and `-v` all print the same default output with no error, so there is no way to discover that those flags do not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `close`, `check` (and ideally `measure`, `version`) to the usage block. Make unknown flags an error rather than a silent no-op, and make `<cmd> --help` print that command's usage.
findings.file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go (usage string near the dispatch switch at line 49)

findings.title: Phase completion is never recorded — every phase reads `running` forever, including after the run is closed
findings.command:
batten phase US-001 research; batten phase US-001 plan; batten phase US-001 build; batten phase US-001 verify; batten phase US-001 close
batten check US-001
batten close US-001
batten show US-001
findings.observed:
US-001  run=US-001-1785219518711611100-3feffc7f  status=ok  phase=close  base=7a332be
  [phase] research                 running 
  [phase] plan                     running 
  [phase] build                    running 
  [phase] verify                   running 
  [phase] close                    running 

verdict qa=ok (batten): all gate checks passed (batten ran them)
findings.expected: Advancing to the next phase marks the previous one done; `batten close` marks the run's phases terminal. A closed run should not display five phases all `running`.
findings.why_it_matters: The run record cannot answer "where did this actually get to?" — the one question it exists to answer. In SQLite every phase node has `ended_at = NULL`; `FinishNode` is never called for phase nodes anywhere in the non-test code. `batten canvas US-001` inherits it verbatim: all five phase cards render `## <phase>\n`running`` on a run whose header says `status ok`. Anyone reading the canvas or the TUI sees a run that is simultaneously finished and entirely in progress.
findings.suggested_fix: In cmdPhase, call FinishNode on the outgoing phase node before starting the new one (status ok, or `blocked` if the phase's gate ended blocked). In cmdClose, finish whatever phase node is still open. Both need the composite-key fix from the node-theft finding first, or they will finish another run's node.

findings.title: doctor's stale-run warning can never be cleared by activity — `events.run_id` is always NULL, so the "no activity" clause is dead code and the message is false
findings.command:
# backdate one open run's started_at by 100h, then:
batten doctor
batten phase US-001 build          # real activity: stamps a new anchor
printf '{"session_id":"sessE","cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | batten hook PreToolUse
batten doctor
findings.observed:
$ batten doctor
⚠ 1 run(s) open >48h with no activity — close or resume them:
    US-001 (phase plan): batten close US-001 [--status ok|failed]

$ batten phase US-001 build
anchor: US-001 base SHA = 70a7179
US-001 -> phase build

$ batten doctor
⚠ 1 run(s) open >48h with no activity — close or resume them:
    US-001 (phase build): batten close US-001 [--status ok|failed]

# events table after all of it:
(None, 'PreToolUse', 1785220052)
(None, 'PreToolUse', 1785220013)
(None, 'SessionStart', 1785219950)
findings.expected: Either the warning clears when the run is worked on (its own advice is "close or resume them"), or it is worded as "opened >48h ago" so the user is not told something false.
findings.why_it_matters: `StaleRuns` computes activity as `COALESCE((SELECT MAX(ts) FROM events e WHERE e.run_id=r.run_id), r.started_at)` (internal/store/store.go:1087), but the only LogEvent call site in the whole non-test codebase passes an empty run id — `h.Store.LogEvent("", "", event, ...)` (internal/hooks/hooks.go:177) — and `nullable("")` turns that into SQL NULL. So the subquery never matches anything and the check degenerates to `started_at < cutoff`. The warning is really "opened >48h ago" and the only way to silence it is to close the run. On a long-lived unit (a two-week epic under active daily work) doctor nags forever and the user learns to ignore it, which is exactly how a real abandoned run then gets missed. It also means the entire events table is orphaned from the run graph — nothing can ever be joined back to a run.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the run in the hook handler (it already does, via activeUnit/EnsureRun) and pass run.RunID to LogEvent. Also bump the run's activity timestamp on `batten phase`, `batten check` and `batten verdict`, so CLI-driven work counts. Until then, reword the message to "opened >48h ago".

findings.title: With two or more open unowned runs the commit gate silently stops enforcing — no deny, no warning, nothing on stdout
findings.command:
export BATTEN_DB=.../run-life/minimal3.db
batten phase FOO-9 build; batten phase us-001 build; batten phase US-1 build   # 3 open, unowned
printf '{"session_id":"newsess","cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git commit -m \"anything\""}}' | batten hook PreToolUse
findings.observed:
--- gate with 3 open unowned runs, unbound session ---
[END OF HOOK OUTPUT -> allow]

(the hook produced zero bytes on stdout and exited 0 — Claude Code reads that as "no opinion", i.e. allow)
findings.expected: At minimum an `additionalContext` / advisory saying "batten cannot tell which unit this commit belongs to — the verdict gate is NOT enforcing; bind this session with `batten phase <unit> <phase>`". Silence here is the one thing the README says batten will never do.
findings.why_it_matters: `activeUnit` deliberately returns "" when ambiguous (internal/hooks/hooks.go:665, comment: "ambiguous: refuse to guess, and refuse to block"), and the SessionStart hook does surface it — but only once, at session start, and only if the user reads the injected context. Every subsequent commit in that session sails through ungated with no output at all. This directly contradicts README.md's core principle that batten fails open only *out loud* ("a gate that silently degrades to trusting the model is worse than no gate, because it will be believed" — a comment the codebase itself writes at hooks.go for the no-checks case, but not for this one). Refusing to guess is right; refusing to say anything is not. Note the interaction with the unit-pattern finding below: junk runs from typos accumulate and are what pushes a repo into this state.
findings.suggested_fix: In the ambiguous branch, emit an `advise()` (the mechanism already used for the gate-with-no-checks case a few lines down) on every gated tool call, not just at SessionStart: name the open units and the exact bind command. Consider also using the commit message's own unit id as a tiebreak before giving up.

findings.title: Unit ids are never validated against the declared `unit.pattern` — a typo opens a permanent phantom run
findings.command:
# batten.yaml declares: unit.pattern = 'US-\d{3}'
batten phase FOO-9 build
batten phase us-001 build
batten phase US-1 build
batten runs
findings.observed:
$ batten phase FOO-9 build
anchor: FOO-9 base SHA = 70a7179
FOO-9 -> phase build
EXIT=0
$ batten phase us-001 build
anchor: us-001 base SHA = 70a7179
us-001 -> phase build
EXIT=0
$ batten phase US-1 build
anchor: US-1 base SHA = 70a7179
US-1 -> phase build
EXIT=0
$ batten runs
UNIT    STATUS   PHASE  VERDICT  TOKENS  IMPUTED
US-1    running  build  —        —       —
us-001  running  build  —        —       —
FOO-9   running  build  —        —       —
findings.expected: `batten: "FOO-9" does not match this project's unit pattern 'US-\d{3}'` and exit 1 — the same courtesy `batten phase US-001 deploy` already gets for an unknown phase (`batten: no phase "deploy" in batten.yaml`).
findings.why_it_matters: `unit.pattern` is described in batten.schema.json as the thing that defines what a unit id is, and `batten phase` — the one command that mints runs — is the only place it is not applied. A lowercase typo (`us-001`) opens a *separate* run that `batten close US-001` will never find, so it stays open forever; each phantom feeds the open-run count that disables the commit gate (previous finding); each also steals the `p-build` phase node from whichever real run held it (first finding). I hit exactly this compound failure by accident: after one stray `batten phase FOO-9 build`, the still-open US-001 run in phase `build` had zero phase nodes and the gate had gone quiet. The strictness the phase-id check already has is the right model.
findings.suggested_fix: In cmdPhase (and cmdClose/cmdCheck/cmdVerdict), run the id through `sp.MatchUnit` / the compiled pattern and reject a non-match, with the pattern quoted in the error and a `--force` escape if genuinely needed.

findings.title: The commit-gate denial names a different unit than the commit message does — the commit text is never consulted
findings.command:
# session sessA is bound to US-001's run; commit message names US-999
printf '{"session_id":"sessA","cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git commit -m \"feat(US-999): nope\""}}' | batten hook PreToolUse
findings.observed: {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"batten: US-001 has no batten-verified pass. The gate's checks must be RUN, not asserted.\nRun: batten check US-001\nTo proceed anyway (recorded): batten override US-001 --reason \"...\""}}
findings.expected: Either resolve the unit from the commit message when it names one, or say so: "this commit names US-999 but this session is bound to US-001".
findings.why_it_matters: batten.schema.json's description of `unit.pattern` says it is "how batten answers 'which unit is this commit for?' without being told" and lists commit messages as one of the places it is matched. In practice `activeUnit` looks only at session binding, then branch name, then the single-unowned-run fallback (internal/hooks/hooks.go:626) — `tool_input.command` is never matched against the pattern. Being told "US-001 has no batten-verified pass" while staring at a commit message that says US-999 reads like a bug in batten, and sends the user off to run `batten check US-001` for a unit they were not working on.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the pattern against the commit message and, on a mismatch with the bound unit, deny with a message that names both. At minimum fix the schema description so it does not promise commit-message resolution.

findings.title: Closed runs are recorded but unreachable — `batten runs` shows two rows for a unit and nothing can inspect the older one
findings.command:
batten runs
batten show US-001 --run US-001-1785219518711611100-3feffc7f
batten show US-001 --json
batten runs --help
findings.observed:
$ batten runs
UNIT    STATUS   PHASE  VERDICT  TOKENS  IMPUTED
US-001  running  plan   —        —       —
US-001  ok       close  ok*      —       —

$ batten show US-001 --run US-001-1785219518711611100-3feffc7f
US-001  run=US-001-1785219778305899600-93c6291a  status=running  phase=plan  base=
(the flag and the run id are both silently ignored — same output as bare `batten show US-001`)

$ batten runs --help
no runs yet
findings.expected: `batten show <unit> --run <run-id>` (or `batten show <run-id>`) opens the historical run; `batten runs` carries a run id / started-at / age column so two rows for one unit are distinguishable; an unrecognised flag is an error.
findings.why_it_matters: The whole value proposition of the run record is that it is durable procedural memory — "the path the work actually took". Once a unit is reopened, the closed run's anchor, verdicts and evidence are permanently invisible from the CLI: `show` and `canvas` both hard-code `LatestRun` (internal/store/store.go:329). `batten runs` gives you two indistinguishable `US-001` rows and no handle to either. `batten budget US-001` is the same problem with a sharper edge: it prints one identical, unlabelled 3-line block per run of that unit, so a unit with two runs prints the same `US-001  0 tokens, $0.00 imputed` block twice with nothing to tell them apart.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `--run <id>` to show/canvas/budget (and accept a bare run id as the positional arg), add a run-id-or-age column to `batten runs`, label each budget block with the run id and status, and reject unknown flags instead of ignoring them.

findings.title: Entering a phase that declares `diff_from: anchor` with no anchor recorded is completely silent
findings.command:
batten phase US-008 plan          # skip build, the phase that carries anchor: git_sha
batten phase US-008 verify        # verify declares diff_from: anchor
