dimension: BUDGET, USAGE ACCOUNTING and "never invent a number"
summary: I copied the template to run-budget/proyecto_ui, declared all three ceilings (tokens_per_run: 200000, imputed_usd_per_run: 2.0, quota_pct_per_run: 15) with on_exceed: block, read internal/usage/usage.go, and hand-built a realistic Claude Code transcript: a parent .jsonl plus two subagent files under <session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl, with replayed multi-content-block lines sharing a requestId, a <synthetic> record carrying 999,999 in/out tokens, an unpriced model, and cache 5m/1h splits. I then drove ingest, budget, measure, statusline, the PreToolUse hook and the MCP server, and cross-checked every number against the SQLite ledger and against prices I computed by hand. Verdict: the accounting CORE is excellent and four of the six claims are proven outright — subagents are counted (a parent-only parser loses 70.1% here), re-ingest is exactly idempotent, quota reports NOT MEASURABLE and never 0 on every surface I could reach, an unmeasurable ceiling never blocks, and measure refuses to conclude below 3 runs per side. My hand-computed total (120,092 tokens, $0.330791) matched batten to the cent. But the surfaces AROUND that core break the project's own first principle in two blocker-grade ways: `batten ingest` silently discards every request timestamped before the run opened and then reports "0 tokens" as if measured (a 291,000-token run reads as pristine and would commit clean), and `on_exceed: block` is silently not enforced at all when the gate declares no `checks:` — a legal spec per batten.schema.json — where a run 7.8x over tokens and 3.5x over dollars committed with only a warning that never mentions the budget. Below that, `batten measure` reports a token column that omits all cache buckets (21.9x understated) next to a dollar column computed on the full basis, prints "$0.00" for an unpriced model with no marker, and presents means over runs whose headroom/code-graph state was never recorded as if they were headroom results.
worked: CLAIM 1 PROVEN — subagent tokens are counted, and a naive parser loses ~70%. Identical parent transcript ingested twice: once with subagents/ present, once absent. `batten ingest US-003 --transcript .../naiveB/ses-nnnn....jsonl` -> `US-003: +3 requests, 35.9k tokens total, $0.15 imputed`; `batten ingest US-004 --transcript .../fullB/ses-ffff....jsonl` -> `US-004: +8 requests, 120.1k tokens total, $0.33 imputed`. The SQLite ledger breaks it down as (parent) 3 req / 35,863 tok, a1b2c3d4 3 req / 66,021 tok, e5f6a7b8 2 req / 18,208 tok — subagents are 84,229 of 120,092 = 70.14% of the run, and 54% of the imputed dollars. batten walks <session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl exactly as documented.

CLAIM 2 PROVEN — re-ingesting does not double-count. Three consecutive identical `batten ingest US-001 --transcript .../ses-aaaa....jsonl`: `+8 requests, 120.1k tokens total, $0.33 imputed`, then `+0 requests, 120.1k tokens total, $0.33 imputed`, then `+0 requests, 120.1k tokens total, $0.33 imputed`. The total is pinned, not incremented — RecordUsage recomputes runs.tokens_spent from the usage table rather than adding to it, so it cannot drift.

Intra-file dedup and synthetic exclusion both work. My parent transcript had three separate lines sharing requestId req_011PARENT02 (the multi-content-block replay the package comments describe) and two sharing req_011SUBA02; the ledger holds exactly one row for each (`select request_id from usage` returns 8 distinct ids for 13 assistant lines). A `<synthetic>` record carrying input_tokens 999999 / output_tokens 999999 was correctly excluded — had it been counted the run would have reported 2.1M tokens instead of 120.1k.

CLAIM 3 PROVEN — quota_pct is reported as NOT MEASURABLE, never as 0, on every surface. CLI: `batten budget US-001` -> `· quota_pct    NOT MEASURABLE — install the statusline (`batten statusline --install`)`. Hook deny text: `    quota_pct    not measurable (install `batten statusline`)` with no `!` marker. MCP `batten_budget` is the best of the three, returning `{"available": false, "exceeded": false, "spent": null, "remaining": null, "unavailable_reason": "the share of the rolling 5-hour subscription window can only be sampled by `batten statusline` ... This ceiling is declared but NOT enforced."}` — null, not zero, plus the reason. `batten doctor` also warns up front: `⚠ budget.quota_pct_per_run is set but the statusline is not installed — that ceiling is NOT enforced.`

CLAIM 4 PROVEN (when the gate declares checks) — exceeding the token ceiling with on_exceed: block really denies the commit through the hook. US-001 at 211,227 / 200,000 tokens, verdict ok with evidence, batten-verified check passed, phase close. Feeding the PreToolUse payload for `git commit -m 'US-001: docker compose'` returned `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"batten: US-001 is over budget. budget.on_exceed=block.
  ! tokens       211227 of 200000
    imputed_usd  $0.39 of $2.00
    quota_pct    not measurable ..."}}`. Only the blown ceiling carries the `!`.

CLAIM 5 PROVEN — an unmeasurable ceiling never causes a block. US-004 at 120.1k/200k tokens and $0.33/$2.00 with quota_pct unmeasurable: the same PreToolUse commit payload returned empty output (no deny). In store.Budget the quota Ceiling is constructed as `{quota_pct, burned, quotaCap, ok && burned >= quotaCap, ok}` — Exceeded is ANDed with measurability, so an unknown quota can never trip OverBudget.

CLAIM 6 PROVEN — `batten measure` says insufficient rather than concluding. With 2 runs on each side: `without code graph   2 run(s): 11.0k tokens, $0.04 imputed (mean)  (insufficient — need ≥3 runs to compare meaningfully)` / `with code graph      2 run(s): 11.0k tokens, $0.04 imputed (mean)  (insufficient — need ≥3 runs to compare meaningfully)`, and the `→ with code graph used X% fewer tokens` conclusion line is correctly withheld.

The quota sensor works end-to-end once a run is unambiguously bound. With one open run, `batten statusline` fed `rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage: 12.0` set the baseline (`· quota_pct    0.0% / 15.0%` — a measured zero, correctly distinct from unknown); a later sample at 31.0 produced `! quota_pct    19.0% / 15.0% of the rolling 5h window` -> `OVER — on_exceed=block`, and the commit was denied on the quota ceiling ALONE with tokens and dollars at zero. Percentage-delta-only, exactly as DESIGN.md argues.

`batten ingest` names unpriced models instead of hiding them: `US-001: +3 requests, 211.2k tokens total, $0.39 imputed` followed by `  unpriced models (counted as $0, tokens still exact): claude-opus-4-9-20260901`.

Pricing is exact and defensible. I priced my transcript by hand from internal/usage/pricing.go (opus 5/25, sonnet-4-5 3/15, haiku 1/5; cache write 5m x1.25, 1h x2.0, read x0.1) and got 120,092 tokens / $0.330791; batten reported 120.1k / $0.33, and the per-agent ledger matched to six decimals (parent 0.15049, a1b2c3d4 0.162663, e5f6a7b8 0.017638). The 5m/1h cache split is priced separately, not collapsed.

The audited escape hatch works: `batten override US-012 --reason "..."` -> `override recorded for US-012 (gate *) ... This override is in the audit log.` and the previously-denied commit then returned empty (allowed).
The schema's underscored-integer form is genuinely accepted: `tokens_per_run: 3_000_000` loads cleanly and renders as `· tokens       0 / 3.0M`. No schema/implementation drift there.

findings.title: `batten measure` reports a headroom / code-graph mean over runs whose flag was never recorded, and drops the "insufficient" caveat once there are 3 of them

batten measure
findings.observed:
headroom effect on THIS project's runs (imputed, not billed):
  unknown              12 run(s): 190.3k tokens, $0.79 imputed (mean)

code graph effect on THIS project's runs (imputed, not billed):
  unknown              4 run(s): 94.9k tokens, $0.22 imputed (mean)
  without code graph   2 run(s): 11.0k tokens, $0.04 imputed (mean)  (insufficient — need ≥3 runs to compare meaningfully)
  with code graph      2 run(s): 11.0k tokens, $0.04 imputed (mean)  (insufficient — need ≥3 runs to compare meaningfully)
findings.expected: The `unknown` bucket should not be rendered as a row under a heading that claims to describe a headroom or code-graph effect — at most a footer such as "4 further runs are excluded: their code-graph state was not recorded". And the whole `headroom effect` section should be suppressed when capabilities.compression is not declared, since batten never probed headroom for any of those runs.
findings.why_it_matters: Both blocks are printed under the heading "<X> effect on THIS project's runs", so `unknown  12 run(s): 190.3k tokens, $0.79 imputed (mean)` reads as a measurement of headroom's effect. It is not: capabilities.compression was never declared, headroomAlive() was never called, and runs.headroom is NULL for all 12. This is a mean over a column that means "we did not look", presented as a result. The caveat logic makes it worse rather than better — it keys off `g.Runs < 3`, so the moment the unknown bucket reaches three runs the "(insufficient)" note disappears and the row stands unqualified. `docs/VERIFICATION.md` claims "con 2 runs dice 'insufficient — need ≥3'; no inventa conclusión", which holds for the with/without rows I proved out, but the unknown row escapes the rule entirely. This is the one command whose stated purpose is to replace vendor claims with the user's own numbers.
findings.file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go — printFlagComparison (~line 600) renders every group including 'unknown'; internal/store/store.go — measureByFlag CASE returns 'unknown' for NULL (~line 975); cmdMeasure calls MeasureByHeadroom unconditionally (~line 588)
findings.suggested_fix: In printFlagComparison, filter the 'unknown' label out of the rendered rows and report it as an excluded-count footer instead. In cmdMeasure, skip the headroom section unless sp.Capabilities.CompressionEnabled() && sp.Capabilities.Compression.Measure, and skip the code-graph section unless sp.Capabilities.GraphEnabled() — the same conditions that decide whether the flag is ever written.

batten · 5h 12% · 7d 34%
US-013  0 tokens, $0.00 imputed
  · quota_pct    NOT MEASURABLE — install the statusline (`batten statusline --install`)

batten · 5h 31% · 7d 35%
US-013  0 tokens, $0.00 imputed
  · quota_pct    NOT MEASURABLE — install the statusline (`batten statusline --install`)
findings.expected: The remedy must name the actual cause. Something like `· quota_pct    NOT MEASURABLE — 2 runs are open and none is bound to a session, so no quota baseline could be attributed. Bind this session (commit or edit a file in the repo) or close the other run.` The statusline is plainly installed and working — it printed `5h 12%` and `5h 31%` on the two lines directly above.

But the message blames the one thing that is demonstrably not wrong, and it is unfalsifiable from the user's side: they run `batten statusline --install`, nothing changes, and there is no further hint. Multiple open runs is the normal state for the fan-out workflow batten is built for, so a user can easily conclude the quota ceiling simply does not work. I only found the real cause by reading `pick`; after closing the other run the identical statusline payloads produced `· quota_pct 0.0% / 15.0%` and then `! quota_pct 19.0% / 15.0%` with a correct commit denial. dimension: OBSERVABILITY — the TUI, canvas, vault, statusline and MCP
summary: I copied the proyecto_ui replica to run-obs/, wrote a batten.yaml (5 phases, 4 domains, gate qa, all three budget ceilings, obsidian vault inside the sandbox) and seeded a realistic US-005 run entirely through the product's own surfaces: `batten phase US-005 build` (anchor 44630cd), three SubagentStart hook payloads across backend/frontend/ml, `batten claim` write-sets for each, three SubagentStop payloads (backend ok, ml failed, frontend ok), a fourth ml subagent as the retry, `batten phase US-005 verify`, and a 3-evidence verdict envelope. Then I exercised every surface: canvas, run note, .base dashboards, index note, budget, show, runs, MCP (real JSON-RPC initialize + tools/list + tools/call on stdin), the TUI both headless and through a real ConPTY, and the statusline with two quota samples. Verdict: the vault layer is the strongest thing here — the run note, the honest "not measured / not zero" language, the danger callout for a missing verdict, the neighbours link and the self-explaining .base dashboards all do exactly what the docs claim, and the statusline quota sensor genuinely works end to end (12% baseline → 29% sample → `OVER BUDGET (quota_pct)` on the line and `! quota_pct 17.0% / 15.0%` in `batten budget`). But the run graph itself has a blocker: node ids are not namespaced per run, so starting the same phase name on a second work item silently deletes the first one's phase node, and the canvas then drops its entire fan-out — US-005's canvas collapsed from 4 nodes/1 edge to a single header card. Alongside that, retries — promised by the README, the vault index note, the canvas colour table and two MCP tool descriptions — have no producer anywhere in the codebase, so no surface can ever show one; and `batten budget` prints the fabricated zero the README explicitly calls "worse than no budget at all", while its own sibling commands report the same fact as unknown.
worked: `batten doctor` reads the sandbox spec and the BATTEN_DB override correctly, and flags both degradations honestly: `⚠ obsidian vault not found: .../run-obs/vault (canvas falls back to .batten/)` and `⚠ budget.quota_pct_per_run is set but the statusline is not installed — that ceiling is NOT enforced. Run: batten statusline --install`.

The .canvas is structurally valid JSON Canvas 1.0. A validator over the 10-node file: `nodes: 10 | unique ids: 10 | duplicates: none`, `invalid node types: none`, `nodes missing x/y/width/height: none`, `nodes with non-positive size: none`, `edges: 4 | unique edge ids: 4`, `dangling edges: none`, `invalid edge sides: none`, `invalid colors: none`. Colours are the spec's preset strings ("1" red for the failed ml agent, "4" green for ok, "6" purple for phases).

The verdict gets its own canvas card with all three evidence items rendered verbatim, sized 380x200 and coloured green — `"id": "verdict", "text": "## verdict: ok

**El esqueleto de OpenTelemetry...**

- pytest backend/tests -q -> 12 passed in 3.4s
- OTel console exporter...
- AC-1 verified: child span db.retrieval present on 3 Polars extractors"`.

Run-note frontmatter is typed exactly as the .base dashboards need it: `verdict: ok`, `evidence_count: 3`, `status: running`, `phase: verify`, `base_sha: 44630cd`, `started: 2026-07-28T06:19:11Z`, `domains: [backend, frontend, ml]` — and `tokens`/`imputed_usd` are OMITTED rather than zeroed. A second unit seeded with no verdict produced `verdict: none` (a real value, not a missing key), which is what makes blocked-verdicts.base able to select it.

The fan-out table shows real write-set sizes, NOT 'not recorded': `| backend | backend | `ok` | 3 files | not measured | not measured |`, `| frontend | frontend | `ok` | 1 file |`, `| ml | ml | `failed` | 2 files |`, `| ml | ml | `ok` | 1 file |`. When I ran a fan-out without claiming, the same cell correctly read `not recorded` — the two states are genuinely distinguished.
Files touched is listed in full (7 paths, deduped and sorted) as inline code rather than wikilinks, exactly as vault.go argues it should be.
The canvas is embedded in the run note with a same-folder link that resolves: `![[US-005.canvas]]`, and the .canvas does sit beside the .md in `vault/batten/proyecto_ui/runs/`.
The 'no verdict' state is the loudest thing in a note, as designed. US-006 rendered `> [!danger] No verdict — the close gate will DENY a commit` with the override escape hatch spelled out.
Neighbour linking is a fact, not a guess: US-006's note emitted `Previous unit: [[US-005]]` only because US-005.md actually exists on disk.
The Stop hook fills the vault by itself — I fired `batten hook Stop` with no `batten canvas` call and US-006.md + US-006.canvas appeared in the vault.

All three .base dashboards plus the index note are present and self-explaining. Each .base carries a header comment (`# A .base is a HUMAN dashboard: its rendered rows are NOT readable by scripts (Obsidian forum #104089). SQLite stays canonical`), all three parse as valid YAML with keys ['filters','properties','views'], and the index note has a 'Reading these numbers' section that explains tokens vs imputed $ vs unmeasurable in plain prose.

`quota_pct` is reported as unmeasurable rather than zero, verbatim as the README promises: `· quota_pct    NOT MEASURABLE — install the statusline (`batten statusline --install`)`. Over MCP the same ceiling returns `"available": false, "spent": null, "remaining": null` with a full `unavailable_reason`.

`batten mcp` speaks real MCP over stdio. An `initialize` on stdin returned `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"capabilities":{"logging":{},"tools":{"listChanged":true}},"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","serverInfo":{"name":"batten","title":"batten — run graph, verdicts, budget","version":"0.1.0"}}}` with instructions attached, and stderr stayed empty (stdout is clean protocol). It exposes exactly 6 tools: batten_runs, batten_run_graph, batten_verdict_status, batten_budget, batten_writeset_owner, batten_spec — each with a full input AND output JSON schema.

`batten_verdict_status` is the best surface in the product. It caught the budget block that no other read-only surface volunteered: `"commit_denied": true, "deny_reason": "US-005 is over budget and budget.on_exceed=block: quota_pct 17.00 of 15.00", "how_to_fix": "raise the ceiling in batten.yaml, or proceed on the record: batten override US-005 --reason \"...\""` — with the full verdict envelope and all 3 evidence strings inline.

`batten_writeset_owner` refuses to guess across open runs and says so: `"note": "several runs are open (US-006, US-005): pass unit or run_id. batten will not guess which one you mean..."`. With an explicit run_id it resolved correctly to `"owner_node": "n-agent-fe-1", "owned_by_you": true`.
Per-node usage on MCP is honest: every node returned `"usage": null` (never `0`), matching the schema's own note 'null means no usage was recorded for this node — not that it cost nothing'.

`batten statusline` works on a real payload. Bare: `batten US-005 verify · verdict ok (3 ev)`. With rate_limits: `batten US-005 verify · verdict ok (3 ev) · quota 0.0/15% · 5h 12% · 7d 32%`. The context segment correctly stayed hidden at 41% and appeared at 86% (`· ctx 86%`).

The quota sensor→budget loop is genuinely closed. After a 12% baseline and a 29% second sample, `batten budget US-005` went from `NOT MEASURABLE` to `! quota_pct    17.0% / 15.0% of the rolling 5h window  [============]` / `OVER — on_exceed=block`, and the status line itself switched to `· OVER BUDGET (quota_pct)`. This is the README's headline budget claim, working.

`batten tui` renders correctly and exits cleanly on `q` when given a real terminal. Driven through a Windows ConPTY at 120x40 it painted a two-pane frame — left: `▸ ◐ US-005    verify`; right: the run header, three budget bars (`tokens ░░░░░░░░ 0 / 3.0M`, `quota ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ 17.0% / 15.0% of the 5h window`, `iters 0 / 3`), the phase tree (`◐ build`, `├─ ✓ backend (backend)  3 files`, `├─ ✗ ml (ml)  2 files`, `└─ ✓ ml (ml)  1 file`), and the full verdict with all 3 evidence lines wrapped — then quit on `q` (probe reported `ALIVE_AFTER_Q=False  BYTES=6839`). The design choice to never truncate the verdict is visible and correct.
`batten runs` and `batten show` report unmeasured usage honestly: `US-005  running  verify  ok  —  —` (em-dashes, not zeros).

findings.why_it_matters: README: 'batten never invents a number. A budget that quietly reports zero for what it failed to measure is worse than no budget at all, because it will be believed.' The MCP tool's own description says 'A ceiling that cannot be measured is reported as unavailable with the reason — never as zero', and its own output schema documents `spent` as 'null when this ceiling cannot be measured — NOT zero'. All three are violated by the same two lines. An unattended `/batten-night` run reading this sees two ceilings with full headroom and 12 empty bar segments and concludes it can keep going, when in fact nothing has been counted. Four surfaces now disagree about one fact, which is the strongest possible signal that the honest ones are accidents rather than policy.
findings.file_hint: internal/store/store.go — Budget(), which hardcodes `true` for the Available field on the tokens and imputed_usd ceilings regardless of whether any usage row exists
findings.suggested_fix: Set Available from whether the run has any usage rows at all (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM usage WHERE run_id=?`), not from whether a cap was declared. The rendering branches in cmd/batten/main.go cmdBudget, internal/hooks/hooks.go formatCeilings and internal/mcp already handle `!Available` correctly — they just never see it.

findings.title: Retries can never be recorded: `retry_of` has four consumers and zero producers, so no surface can show a retry the README, the vault index and two MCP tools all promise
findings.command:
# seed a genuine retry: ml agent fails, a second ml agent fixes it
echo '{..."hook_event_name":"SubagentStop","agent_id":"agent-ml-1","last_assistant_message":"error: ... the run failed."}' | batten hook SubagentStop
echo '{..."hook_event_name":"SubagentStart","agent_id":"agent-ml-2","agent_type":"ml"}' | batten hook SubagentStart
echo '{..."hook_event_name":"SubagentStop","agent_id":"agent-ml-2","last_assistant_message":"Retry: async-generator span wrapper...; 6 tests pass."}' | batten hook SubagentStop
batten canvas US-005
batten --help | grep -i retry
grep -rn 'AddEdge' --include=*.go .   # in the batten source tree
findings.observed:
# the two ml nodes in the canvas are indistinguishable apart from colour:
{"id":"n-agent-ml-1",...,"color":"1","text":"**ml**\ndomain: `ml`\n`failed`"}
{"id":"n-agent-ml-2",...,"color":"4","text":"**ml**\ndomain: `ml`\n`ok`"}
# all 4 edges are spawn; there is no retry_of edge and no Relations section in the run note.

# MCP batten_run_graph on the run that contained the retry:
"retries": 0

# batten --help has no retry/edge/link command.
# the only edge producer in the entire codebase:
./internal/hooks/hooks.go:494:  _ = h.Store.AddEdge(run.RunID, "p-"+run.Phase, nodeID, "spawn")
findings.expected: A retry is visible as a retry. The README says the canvas draws 'the phases, the fan-out, the retries, the blocked verdict that got fixed and re-verified'; the vault index note batten itself writes says 'as it actually happened: the phases, the fan-out, the retries'; batten_run_graph's description says 'the TYPED edges between them (spawn, depends_on, retry_of, rollback) ... including retries and rollbacks'; canvas.go has a `relColor("retry_of") -> orange` branch.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most-advertised property of the run graph and it cannot happen. Four consumers exist — canvas.go relColor, vault.go renderRelations, mcp.go's `retries` counter, tui.go's cross-edge rendering — and no code path in the binary, the hooks or the plugin's skills ever writes anything but a `spawn` edge. `depends_on`, `supersedes` and `rollback` are in the same position. I proved the renderers are fine by injecting one row by hand into a copy of the DB: the run note immediately produced '## Relations / - `retry_of`: ml → ml'. So the whole gap is a missing producer. Until then, a user looking at two red-and-green `ml` cards has no way to know the second is the retry of the first rather than a second independent ml task, and `retries: 0` is an actively wrong answer given to the agent.
findings.file_hint: internal/hooks/hooks.go subagentStart (the natural place to emit it) and cmd/batten/main.go (no command exists)
findings.suggested_fix: Cheapest honest fix: add `batten retry <new-agent-id> --of <old-agent-id>` calling AddEdge(run, new, old, "retry_of"), and have /batten-build's fix loop call it. Better: have SubagentStart accept an optional `retry_of` agent id, or infer it — a new subagent with the same agent_type in the same phase as a node whose status is `failed` is a retry with high confidence. Also give the two cards distinguishable text (append the agent_id or an attempt number; the `attempt` column already exists in the nodes schema and is never used).

findings.title: A retry cannot claim the files it must fix — the failed agent still owns them and there is no way to release a write-set
findings.command:
# agent-ml-1 failed while owning ml/data/extractors.py; agent-ml-2 is its retry
batten claim agent-ml-2 ml/data/extractors.py ml/data/spans.py
findings.observed:
batten: write-set collision: ml/data/extractors.py is already owned by n-agent-ml-1
# exit=1

# and there is no release/unclaim command:
batten --help   ->  init, doctor, hook, phase, claim, verdict, runs, show, canvas, budget, override, tui, mcp, statusline, ingest
findings.expected: A retry of a failed agent inherits (or can take over) that agent's write-set. Failing that, a clear error explaining how to hand the fence over — `batten claim --release`, `batten claim --supersede <old-agent>`, or an automatic transfer when the previous owner's node status is `failed`.
findings.why_it_matters: The retry is the whole point of the run graph, and the product cannot execute one without either abandoning the files that failed or hand-editing SQLite. I only got a retry into the graph at all by giving the second ml agent a different file. The guard is right to be strict — that fence is the feature — but a failed, finished node holding a permanent lock is not the disjointness rule, it is a leak: the owner is dead and nothing reclaims it. This is also what makes finding #4 unfixable in practice even if the edge existed.
findings.file_hint: internal/store/store.go ClaimWriteSet (rejects any second owner unconditionally) and cmd/batten/main.go cmdClaim
findings.suggested_fix: Allow a claim to take over a path whose current owner node has status `failed` (or `ended_at IS NOT NULL`), recording a `retry_of`/`supersedes` edge as the audit trail — which would produce the missing edge from finding #4 for free. Alternatively add an explicit `batten claim --from <old-agent-id>` transfer that is refused unless the old node is finished.

agent-fe-1 owns 1 file(s); any other agent writing them is now denied

- `frontend/composables/usetrace.ts`

findings.why_it_matters: Three observability surfaces report a path that does not exist in the repository. On the human side the run note's 'Files touched' is the audit trail of what the fan-out did, and it names a file git has never heard of — on a case-sensitive CI checkout `usetrace.ts` is simply a different file. On the agent side it is worse: a fanned-out subagent told 'your write-set is frontend/composables/usetrace.ts' and instructed to stay inside its fence will create a second, wrongly-cased file. If a schema change is too invasive right now, at minimum stop folding in the read paths' display and note the limitation.

findings.title: Phase nodes are never finished, so the canvas and TUI paint every phase as `running` forever
findings.command:
batten phase US-005 build      # ... fan-out completes ...
batten phase US-005 verify
batten canvas US-005 && grep -o '## build[^"]*' vault/.../US-005.canvas
findings.expected: `## build` / `ok` in green once the run has moved past it, matching how subagent nodes already transition from `running` to `ok`/`failed` via FinishNode.
findings.why_it_matters: Colour is the fastest signal on the canvas, and it says nothing: every phase is purple regardless of what happened. A user scanning a finished run cannot tell which phases completed, and a run that ended three days ago still reads as in-flight. `FinishNode` has exactly one caller in the whole codebase (SubagentStop), and neither `SetPhase` nor `CloseRun` touches the nodes table, so a phase node's status is written once at creation and never again.
findings.file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go cmdPhase (creates the new phase node without closing the previous one) and internal/store/store.go CloseRun (updates runs only)
findings.suggested_fix: In cmdPhase, before adding the new phase node, call FinishNode on the run's previous phase node with status `ok`. In CloseRun, finish any still-running phase node of that run with the run's final status.

dimension: THE FROM-ZERO DEMO REPO — building a real repo and walking the five-step adoption path end to end
summary: I built a real Go service (`taskly`: `store/` owns task state and validation, `api/` is HTTP in front of it, 9 stdlib-only tests, no Makefile, no network) at $SANDBOX/batten-testbed/demo-batten-quickstart, and walked the adoption path from `git init` with BATTEN_DB pointed at the repo's own .batten-demo.db. The core product works and works well: `batten init` found both domains and wrote correct `go` check commands; `batten doctor` validated the spec and caught a dangling `reads:`, a missing rules file and an uninstalled skill; `batten check` really ran `go vet`/`go test` through `cmd /C` on Windows and recorded machine-generated evidence; the commit gate DENIED on a blocked verdict and ALLOWED after the fix; `result:"ok"` with an empty `evidence[]` was rejected with exit 1; the write-set guard denied a cross-fence Edit and allowed an in-fence one. The demo deliberately fails by breaking a declared invariant (the trim goes in `api/` instead of `store/`), which is reversible with `git apply [-R] scripts/break-the-invariant.patch`. The verdict on the from-zero path itself is worse than the verdict on the product: the gate does not exist until some batten command has created a run for the unit, so the very first commit after adoption sails through silently — and the unit id is read only from the branch name, so a trunk-based repo gets no gate and no warning. On top of that, the two commands the path actually needs (`batten check`, `batten close`) are in neither `--help` nor the README, `doctor` and `check` both exit 0 on failure, and `batten init --help` writes a file. IMPORTANT: the prebuilt binary (23:52) predates two source fixes (d99b6ef 00:07, 3122d29 00:07), so I discarded two candidate findings — init suggesting skills by prose match (`skills: [gsap-core]` on an `api/` domain) and init not reading docs/backlog.md for the unit pattern — both already fixed at HEAD. Every finding below I re-verified against HEAD source (64d1d55) as well as reproducing it live. Isolation held: BATTEN_DB was honoured on every command after the first probe, no remote was added, proyecto_ui and the Obsidian vault were never written.
worked: `batten init` on a virgin Go repo: detected both domains from the layout (`api/`, `store/`), pointed each at its own AGENTS.md, wrote `check: ['go build ./...', 'go vet ./...', 'go test ./...']`, defaulted to `enforcement: report`, and listed its own guesses under a '# --- things to decide ---' block. Output: `wrote batten.yaml — a working draft in report mode (gates warn, don't block).  project="demo-batten-quickstart" unit="TASK", 2 domain(s) detected`
`batten init` refuses to clobber an existing spec: `batten: batten.yaml already exists — remove it or edit it by hand` (exit 1)

`BATTEN_DB` is honoured by every command and `batten doctor` prints the path it is using, so the sandboxing is verifiable: `✓ store: .../demo-batten-quickstart/.batten-demo.db`. The user's real ~/.batten/batten.db was never written by my commands.
`batten doctor` on the edited spec: 4 clean lines including `✓ close gate: phase "close" requires verdict "ok" on any gate` and `✓ enforcement: enforce — gates block`

`batten doctor` catches real spec errors: `- phase "verify" reads "nonexistent_artifact", which is neither an artifact nor a prior phase`, `- phase "verify" references unknown gate "no-such-gate"`, `⚠ domain "api": rules file missing: api/DOES-NOT-EXIST.md`, `⚠ domains.api.skills references "no-such-skill-anywhere", which is not installed`
`batten phase TASK-001 build` records the anchor exactly as documented: `anchor: TASK-001 base SHA = 19ba13a`

`batten check` runs the gate commands for real on Windows (via `cmd /C`) and inlines the failing test output: `✗ go test ./... (exit 1)` followed by the two real `--- FAIL:` lines, then `TASK-001: BLOCKED (batten-verified). one or more gate checks failed`. The evidence it stores is generated, not typed: `- go vet ./...: PASS (exit 0, 691ms)` / `- go test ./...: PASS (exit 0, 2.631s)`

THE VERDICT GATE — DENY. `batten hook PreToolUse` with a `git commit` payload returned `{"permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"batten: TASK-001 verdict is \"blocked\", not \"ok\". one or more gate checks failed\nsafe_next_step: fix the failures, then run batten check again\nTo proceed anyway (recorded): batten override TASK-001 --reason \"...\""}`

THE EVIDENCE RULE. `echo '{"check_id":"TASK-001-qa","result":"ok","evidence":[]}' | batten verdict --unit TASK-001` → `batten: result "ok" with an empty evidence[] is not allowed: an approval must cite something (command output, test counts, a criterion verified). Without evidence the result is "blocked"` — exit 1, rejected before the DB. This is the one command in the CLI that exits non-zero on failure.

THE VERDICT GATE — ALLOW. After the fix and `batten verdict --unit TASK-001 --file verdict.json` → `verdict recorded: TASK-001 qa=ok (5 evidence)`, the identical hook payload returned empty output / exit 0 and the real `git commit` succeeded: `a5dd760 feat(TASK-001): reject blank task titles in the store`

THE WRITE-SET GUARD. `batten claim node-1a/store store/store.go store/store_test.go` → `node-1a/store owns 2 file(s); any other agent writing them is now denied`; a PreToolUse Edit from `node-2b/api` on `store/store.go` → `deny` with `batten: write-set collision. store/store.go belongs to another agent's write-set ...; If this file genuinely belongs to you, the plan is wrong: fix the plan, do not cross the fence.` An Edit on its own `api/handler_test.go` was allowed (empty output).
`batten close TASK-001` → `TASK-001 closed (ok). Write-set claims released — files it held are free again.` and `batten runs` correctly flips to `STATUS ok`

The two-source verdict model is genuinely good design and is visible in the output: `batten check` writes `verdict qa=ok (batten)` with real command results, and `batten verdict --file` writes `verdict qa=ok (agent)` with the reviewer's acceptance-criteria judgment.

findings.command: cd demo-batten-quickstart && git checkout -b feature/TASK-002 && printf '{"session_id":"newcomer-session","hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","cwd":"<repo>","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git commit -m \\"feat(TASK-002): mark a task done\\""}}' | batten hook PreToolUse; echo "exit=$?"

(no output at all)
exit=0

$ batten runs
UNIT      STATUS   PHASE  VERDICT  TOKENS  IMPUTED
TASK-001  running  close  ok       —       —
findings.expected: A deny, or at minimum a visible warning. The README's headline scene is 'an agent finishes a work item, feels good about it, and reaches for the commit -> permission denied'. They conclude batten is installed and working — it is installed and doing nothing. The gate only ever fires for units someone already ran `batten phase` or `batten check` on, which is precisely the disciplined case that needed the gate least. It also means the whole product can be bypassed by never touching the CLI.

  batten ingest <unit> --transcript  price a transcript's tokens into the run ledger
findings.expected: `main()` dispatches `check`, `close`, `measure` and `hook-debug`; none appear in printUsage() and none appear in README.md. `batten check` is the command that runs the gate's checks, generates the machine evidence, and turns a blocked verdict into ok — it is the single highest-value verb in the binary. `batten close` is the only way to move a run out of `status=running`.
findings.why_it_matters: A newcomer who follows the README gets as far as a denied commit and then has no documented way forward except `batten override`. The literal instruction in the deny message is 'fix the failures, then run batten check again' — a command that does not exist as far as `--help` and the README are concerned. I only found it by probing the binary with a bad subcommand and then reading cmd/batten/main.go.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `batten check [<unit>] [--gate <name>]  run the gate's checks and record the evidence` and `batten close <unit> [--status ok|blocked]  finish the unit and release its write-set claims` to printUsage(), and put `batten check` into the README's five-step path — it is the step between 'work a unit' and 'commit'.

findings.title: `batten check` exits 0 when the unit is BLOCKED
findings.command: cd demo-batten-quickstart && git apply scripts/break-the-invariant.patch && batten check; echo "exit=$?"
findings.observed:
✓ go vet ./...
  ✗ go test ./... (exit 1)
    --- FAIL: TestAddRejectsBlankTitle (0.00s)
    --- FAIL: TestAddTrimsTitle (0.00s)
    FAIL

TASK-001: BLOCKED (batten-verified). one or more gate checks failed
the commit gate will deny until this passes.
exit=0
findings.expected: A non-zero exit when the result is `blocked`. The message even says 'the commit gate will deny until this passes' — the process then reports success to its caller.
findings.why_it_matters: `batten check && git commit` commits a blocked unit. So does any CI step, Makefile target, pre-commit hook or shell one-liner that chains on the exit status — which is the natural way anyone would wire a check command. The hook gate would still catch it inside Claude Code, but outside Claude Code (a terminal, CI) `batten check` is the only enforcement available and it reports pass on fail.
findings.suggested_fix: In cmdCheck, after printing the summary, `if result != "ok" { return errors.New(...) }` — or add an explicit sentinel that main() maps to exit 1 without double-printing.

findings.title: `batten doctor` exits 0 on an invalid spec
findings.command:
mkdir repro && cd repro && git init -q -b main . && cat > batten.yaml <<'EOF'
version: 1
project: repro
unit: {name: TASK, pattern: 'TASK-\d{3}'}
phases:
  - id: verify
    gate: no-such-gate
  - id: close
    requires_verdict: ok
EOF
batten doctor; echo "exit=$?"
findings.observed:
✗ .../repro/batten.yaml: invalid spec:
  - phase "verify" references unknown gate "no-such-gate"
exit=0
findings.expected: Non-zero. A validator that prints ✗ and returns success cannot be used as a validator. The same holds for `✗ no batten.yaml found. Run: batten init` (also exit 0).
findings.why_it_matters: `batten doctor` is the natural CI guard — 'the spec still parses' is exactly the thing you want to break a build. As shipped, a `batten doctor` step in CI passes on a spec that the loader will refuse at runtime, so a broken batten.yaml lands on main and the failure surfaces at 3am in the hook instead.
findings.suggested_fix: cmdDoctor should return the error instead of `fmt.Printf` + `return nil` in the two `✗` branches. If a zero exit is wanted for the 'no spec here' case specifically, keep that one at 0 and make 'invalid spec' non-zero — but do not print ✗ and succeed.

findings.title: `batten init --help` writes batten.yaml instead of printing help — unknown flags are silently ignored on every subcommand
findings.command: mkdir fresh && cd fresh && git init -q -b main . && ls && batten init --help; echo "exit=$?"; ls
findings.observed:
(dir was empty)
wrote batten.yaml — a working draft in report mode (gates warn, don't block).
  project="repro" unit="TASK", 0 domain(s) detected, graphify found, engram found
Next:
  1. fill the invariants (the TODOs) — the highest-value part of the file
  2. run: batten doctor
  3. flip enforcement: enforce when you trust the gates
exit=0
files now:
batten.yaml
findings.expected: Usage text for `init`, exit 0 or 2. Asking a command for help should never mutate the working tree. cmdInit's arg loop recognises only `--scan-json` and `--from` and drops everything else on the floor; the same pattern is in cmdCheck, cmdClose, cmdVerdict.
findings.why_it_matters: `--help` on a subcommand is the first thing anyone types. Here it creates a file. In a repo that already had a batten.yaml it merely errors, but in a fresh repo — exactly the from-zero case — you get an unrequested spec you did not read. It also means a typo'd flag (`--form docs/workflow.md`) is silently ignored rather than reported, so `batten init --form ...` writes a spec that migrated nothing and says nothing about it. I hit this myself on my very first command against the binary.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each subcommand a real flag.FlagSet (which handles -h/--help and rejects unknown flags), or at minimum add a `default:` arm in each hand-rolled loop that errors on any argument starting with `--` that it does not recognise.
findings.file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go:1429-1440 (cmdInit's arg loop has no default arm); same shape at 646-659 (cmdClose) and 724-737 (cmdCheck)

findings.title: Phases never reach a terminal state — every phase still reads `running` after the unit is closed ok
findings.command: batten phase TASK-001 plan && batten phase TASK-001 build && batten phase TASK-001 verify && batten phase TASK-001 close && batten close TASK-001 && batten show TASK-001
findings.observed:
TASK-001 closed (ok). Write-set claims released — files it held are free again.

TASK-001  run=TASK-001-1785219713838879200-01e63c19  status=ok  phase=close  base=19ba13a
  [phase] plan                     running 
  [phase] build                    running 
  [phase] verify                   running 
  [phase] close                    running 
  [subagent] general-purpose          running  owns 2 file(s)
  [subagent] general-purpose          running  owns 1 file(s)
findings.expected: `plan`, `build` and `verify` should be done/ok once the run advanced past them, and all four should be terminal once `batten close` set `status=ok`. `batten phase <unit> <next>` advances the pointer but never closes out the phase it left.
findings.why_it_matters: `batten show` is the human's window onto what actually happened, and it reports a finished, approved, committed unit as four phases still in flight. The same state feeds `batten canvas`, so the Obsidian view is wrong in the same way. A reviewer cannot tell a run that stalled in `verify` from one that sailed through all four.
findings.suggested_fix: In cmdPhase, mark the previous phase node done when advancing; in cmdClose, mark every remaining phase node terminal with the run's status.
findings.file_hint: cmd/batten/main.go cmdPhase / cmdClose, and the phase node status column in internal/store

findings.title: `batten canvas` draws no edges between phases — the 'run DAG' is a row of disconnected boxes
findings.command: batten canvas TASK-001   # after a complete run: 4 phases, 2 subagents, a blocked verdict then an ok one
findings.observed:
wrote .../.batten/TASK-001.canvas (12 nodes, 2 edges)

$ python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.batten/TASK-001.canvas'));[print(e['fromNode'],'->',e['toNode']) for e in d['edges']]"
p-close -> n-node-1a/store
p-close -> n-node-2b/api
findings.expected: Edges for `plan -> build -> verify -> close` at minimum. The README says the canvas 'draws the path the work actually took, not the one the plan hoped for' — with no phase-to-phase edges there is no path drawn at all, only x-coordinates. (Before the subagents existed it was literally `10 nodes, 0 edges`.)
findings.why_it_matters: The canvas is the project's only visual artefact and the reason JSON Canvas was chosen ('zero lines of graph-layout code on our side. Obsidian already renders it'). Obsidian renders four unconnected group boxes, all labelled `running`. The retries, the blocked-then-fixed verdict, the ordering — none of it is expressed as graph structure.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit an edge between consecutive phase nodes in spec order, and an edge from the verdict node to the phase whose gate it satisfies. Colour the edge by the phase's terminal status once that lands (previous finding).

findings.title: `batten budget` prints `0 tokens, $0.00` for a run it never measured — the exact failure the README says it refuses to commit
findings.command: batten budget TASK-001   # on a run with no ingested transcript
findings.expected: Something that distinguishes 'measured, and it was zero' from 'never measured'. The README is emphatic about this: 'batten never invents a number. A budget that quietly reports zero for what it failed to measure is worse than no budget at all, because it will be believed.' It even shows the right pattern for quota: `NOT MEASURABLE — install the statusline`. The token ledger gets no such treatment.
findings.why_it_matters: The whole point of the budget section is that an unattended overnight run needs a tripwire you can trust. Empty progress bars at 0/3.0M read as 'you have used nothing, keep going' — which is what an unattended run would conclude — when the truth is 'nothing was ever counted'. `batten runs` gets this right in the same session, printing `—` for TOKENS and IMPUTED; `batten budget` should agree with it.
findings.suggested_fix: When the ledger has no ingested transcript for the run, print `tokens  NOT MEASURED — run: batten ingest <unit> --transcript <path>` instead of `0 / 3.0M`, matching the quota_pct line's existing honesty.

findings.title: `batten doctor` never checks that the `check:` / `gates.checks` commands can actually run
findings.command:
# batten.yaml with:  check: ['this-command-does-not-exist --at-all']  and the same under gates.qa.checks
batten doctor
findings.observed:
✓ .../batten.yaml — project "probe", unit "TASK", 3 phases, 1 domains
✓ close gate: phase "close" requires verdict "ok" on any gate
✓ enforcement: enforce — gates block
✓ store: .../probe.db
⚠ domain "api": rules file missing: api/DOES-NOT-EXIST.md
⚠ domains.api.skills references "no-such-skill-anywhere", which is not installed
findings.expected: A warning that the check command is not resolvable, in the same family as the two warnings it does emit. batten.schema.json makes this the governing rule for the field: 'Take them verbatim from the Makefile / package.json — do not invent a command that does not exist in the repo.' doctor verifies the rules file and the skill name, which are cheaper mistakes, but not the commands the gate's entire credibility rests on.
findings.why_it_matters: `batten init` guesses these commands heuristically, and the newcomer's job in step 3 is to confirm them. A typo (`go tst ./...`, `make check` in a repo with no Makefile) produces a clean doctor and then a permanently-blocked unit at commit time, or worse, a green run in a repo where `make` silently no-ops. Resolving argv[0] is a two-line check.
findings.suggested_fix: For each domain check and gate check, split off argv[0] and `exec.LookPath` it (plus a `./`-relative file check), warning `⚠ gate "qa": check "..." — command "go tst" not found on PATH`. Do not run the command, just resolve it.

findings.title: `batten init` neither creates a .gitignore nor adds `.batten/`, which `batten canvas` then writes into the repo
findings.command: batten init && batten canvas TASK-001 && git status --short
findings.observed:
wrote .../demo-batten-quickstart/.batten/TASK-001.canvas (10 nodes, 0 edges)

$ git status --short
?? .batten/
findings.expected: `batten init`, which already writes a file into the repo, should also ensure `.batten/` is ignored — or `batten canvas` should default somewhere outside the tree. The canvas is a rendered view of a database, not source.
findings.why_it_matters: The default `batten canvas <unit>` path drops a generated artefact into the working tree with no mention of it. On a team, everyone's canvas lands in `git status` and eventually in a commit, then conflicts on regeneration. It is a one-line fix at the exact moment batten already has the repo open for writing.
findings.suggested_fix: In cmdInit, append `.batten/` to .gitignore (creating it if absent) and say so in the 'Next:' block. Mention the canvas output path in `--help`.

findings.title: `batten doctor` stops at the first fatal validation error and never reaches its warnings, so fixing a spec is one round-trip per problem
findings.command:
# spec with ALL of: a bad `reads:` ref, a missing rules file, an uninstalled skill, a nonexistent check command
batten doctor
# then remove only the bad `reads:` line and run it again
findings.observed:
first run:
✗ .../batten.yaml: invalid spec:
  - phase "verify" reads "nonexistent_artifact", which is neither an artifact nor a prior phase

second run (after fixing only that one line):
✓ .../batten.yaml — project "probe", unit "TASK", 3 phases, 1 domains
...
⚠ domain "api": rules file missing: api/DOES-NOT-EXIST.md
⚠ domains.api.skills references "no-such-skill-anywhere", which is not installed
findings.expected: One report listing everything doctor knows about the file. The two warnings were true on the first run and were withheld. The loader already accumulates its own errors into a list ('invalid spec:' with a bullet per problem), so this is only about doctor abandoning the run when Load fails.
findings.why_it_matters: Step 3 of the adoption path is 'edit the draft init wrote' — the one step where a newcomer makes several mistakes at once. Getting them one at a time, each costing a full read-edit-run cycle, is the difference between a five-minute setup and a twenty-minute one. Minor, but it lands squarely on the first impression.
findings.suggested_fix: When spec.Load fails, print the fatal errors and then continue with whatever file-level checks do not need a loaded Spec (rules files, skill names, check-command resolution) parsed straight from the YAML.

findings.title: The internal `n-` node prefix leaks into the write-set denial message the agent reads
findings.command:
batten claim node-1a/store store/store.go store/store_test.go
printf '{..."agent_id":"node-2b/api","tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<repo>/store/store.go"}}' | batten hook PreToolUse
findings.observed: batten: write-set collision. store/store.go belongs to another agent's write-set (n-node-1a/store); you are n-node-2b/api.
findings.expected: `(node-1a/store); you are node-2b/api` — the ids the user typed into `batten claim` and the ones the plugin passes as `agent_id`. The README's own example shows `(node-7f3a/ml-C); you are node-2b91/ml-A`, with no prefix.
findings.why_it_matters: The denial message is one of exactly two user-facing outputs the whole product is built around, and it prints an id that matches nothing the user can grep for — not the claim they made, not the agent_id in the hook payload, not the README. It reads like a second, mangled identifier and invites the reader to wonder which one is real.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip the node-table prefix when formatting the collision message (or store the display id alongside the node id).

findings.title: `batten claim` cannot be used from a terminal at all, and its usage line does not say why
findings.command: batten claim node-1a/store store/store.go store/store_test.go   # in a repo with a valid spec and an active run
findings.observed:
batten: no subagent "node-1a/store" on record; the SubagentStart hook creates it
exit=1
findings.expected: Either it works, or `batten --help` says it is not a standalone command. The usage line reads `batten claim <agent-id> <file>...  declare a subagent's write-set`, with nothing to suggest the agent must already have been registered by a SubagentStart hook that only Claude Code fires.
findings.why_it_matters: The error message is good — it names the cause — but it arrives after the user has already been told, by --help, that this is a command they can run. To demo or debug the write-set guard outside a live fan-out you have to hand-craft a SubagentStart payload and pipe it into `batten hook SubagentStart` first, which requires reading internal/hooks/hooks.go to learn the field names. I did exactly that to produce the demo.
findings.suggested_fix: Annotate the usage line: `batten claim <agent-id> <file>...  declare a write-set (the agent must exist: fan-out only)`. Optionally let `claim` create the subagent row itself when given `--register`, which would make the guard demonstrable from a terminal.
